NDC hails court order on party logo
items.description: —Directs members to use approved two-finger logo By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has hailed the Judiciary for directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise and use the party’s modified digital logo. The party also directed all its candidates and members to use only the approved NDC logo on campaign materials, including banners, posters and other publicity items. In a statement on Thursday, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said the Federal High Court sitting in Abuja granted the party’s prayers in a suit seeking to compel INEC to upload and use its modified digital logo as contained in the party’s constitution. The party said the modified logo was to replace the old association logo with which the NDC was originally registered. According to the statement, the NDC approved the modified logo at its first National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting on March 25, 2026, and subsequently forwarded it to INEC. The party said INEC initially uploaded the new logo but later removed it and reinstated the old association logo without communicating any reason to the party. The NDC said it gave the electoral commission sufficient time to resolve the issue administratively but was eventually compelled to seek legal redress. In a judgment delivered by Justice J.O. Abdulmalik, the court ordered INEC to approve the modified logo design, including its symbol and colours, for use by the NDC as its official logo for all purposes as a political party, including elections conducted by the commission. The court also granted an order of perpetual injunction restraining INEC from stopping or interfering with the NDC’s use of the digitally designed “two-finger” victory sign. The party described the judgment as a timely intervention by the Judiciary and thanked the court for directing INEC to recognise its modified logo. Against this backdrop, the NDC directed all candidates and members to adopt and use only the approved logo on campaign materials and other party publicity items. The party acknowledged that some candidates and members might have already produced campaign materials bearing the old logo, and regretted any inconvenience caused by the change. It said it would intensify public sensitisation on the party’s official logo and urged its supporters and candidates not to be worried by the development. “We assure our supporters and candidates that there is nothing to worry about. We are in this together,” the statement added. The post NDC hails court order on party logo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dumelo wishes NSMQ finalists well ahead of contest
items.description: Member of Parliament for Ayawaso West Wuogon, John Dumelo and Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture has wished the three finalists of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) well ahead of today’s grand finale. Presbyterian Boys’ Secondary School (PRESEC-Legon), St Augustine’s College and Accra Academy will battle for the 2026 NSMQ crown at the University of Ghana Premier Dome at 3:00 pm. Mr Dumelo, speaking ahead of the contest, said he was wishing all three schools the best, although he jokingly ruled out Accra Academy’s chances of winning the competition. “Accra Academy will not win,” he said, adding that the school “doesn’t fit.” Accra Academy is appearing in the NSMQ grand finale for the first time, while PRESEC-Legon, an eight-time champion, returns to the final after a two-year absence in search of a record ninth title. St Augustine’s College, a two-time champion, is also seeking to add a third title to its collection. Mr Dumelo acknowledged Accra Academy’s historic qualification and said the school could still produce a surprise in the final. He also welcomed the return of the grand finale to the constituency, describing it as “good” and “great” and expressing hope that more major events would be hosted there. He, however, declined to make any promises to the participating schools or students, joking that his “mommy finish” and he could no longer make promises.

items.title: Let your reasoning and fairness define your legacy – Mahama to new justices
items.description: President John Mahama has urged three newly sworn-in Supreme Court justices to remain independent and allow the quality of their reasoning, fairness of their decisions, and loyalty to the Constitution to define their legacy. Speaking at the swearing-in ceremony on Thursday, September 10, at the Jubilee House, President Mahama said the justices must instead focus on the quality of their legal reasoning and the fairness of their judgments. “Let the quality of your reasoning define your legacy, the fairness of your decisions, and your unwavering loyalty to the Constitution,” he said. President Mahama cautioned the justices against allowing public pressure, political interests, or criticism to influence their decisions, particularly in cases that attract strong emotions. “You will sometimes be called upon to decide matters that generate strong public emotions and competing political interests,” he said. “In those moments, you must remain unmoved by the pressures, the praise, or the criticism. Do not allow yourselves to be defined by the individuals, governments, or institutions that appear before you.” He reminded the justices that their decisions could have a direct impact on the lives of ordinary Ghanaians, stressing that every case before the court involves people whose rights and future may be at stake. “Remember, always, that behind every case file are human beings whose rights, livelihoods, freedoms, and futures may depend upon your judgments,” President Mahama said. He urged them to approach their work with humility and patience while taking the time to examine the law carefully before reaching their decisions. “Approach every matter with humility. Listen patiently. Examine the law carefully. Decide courageously,” he said. The President further urged the justices to make justice and the national interest the guiding principles of their work. “And let justice and the national interests remain your abiding purpose,” he added. President Mahama told the newly appointed justices that their elevation to the Supreme Court placed a significant responsibility on them, given the trust the Ghanaian people had placed in the judiciary. In congratulating Justice Sophia Rosetta Bernasko Essah, Justice Edward Amoako Asante and Anthony Forson Jnr, he urged them to serve with wisdom, integrity and independence. “Justice Benas Kuesa, Justice Edward Amakwa Asante, and Justice Anthony Fawcett, Jr., the people of Ghana have entrusted you with an enormous responsibility. May you serve with wisdom, integrity, and independence,” he said. He said the work of the three justices should contribute to strengthening Ghana’s democracy and the rule of law, while ensuring that vulnerable people are protected. “May your judgments deepen our democracy, protect the vulnerable, and strengthen the rule of law,” President Mahama said. He ended by congratulating the three justices and wishing them a successful and distinguished tenure on the Supreme Court. “On behalf of the government and people of Ghana, I congratulate you and wish you a successful and distinguished tenure on the Supreme Court of Ghana,” he said.

items.title: FG scraps data charges for students
items.description: …moves to regulate internet access for under-16s By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government on Thursday unveiled a major digital education intervention that will allow millions of Nigerian students to access approved educational platforms without paying for internet data, in a move aimed at dismantling one of the biggest barriers to technology-driven learning in the country. The initiative, unveiled by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, under the Initiative for Zero-Rated Access to Educational Platforms and Content in Nigeria, is designed to make digital learning accessible to children and young people regardless of their economic circumstances or location. But while announcing the removal of data costs for approved educational content, Alausa also revealed that the government was working towards regulated internet access for children below 16 years, signalling a dual approach of expanding digital access while tightening protection for young users in the online environment. The minister, who spoke at the launch of the initiative, said the government was determined to ensure that the cost of internet connectivity no longer determined which Nigerian child could access quality educational resources. According to him, the initiative was not merely about providing connectivity but about ensuring that learning remained within the reach of children who could otherwise be shut out because of the cost of data. “This initiative goes beyond connectivity. It is about putting learning within reach of children who may otherwise be unable to afford the data required to access it,” Alausa said. The minister’s announcement comes at a time when Nigeria is battling a huge education deficit, with millions of children out of school and many others struggling with inadequate learning facilities, poor connectivity, unreliable electricity and limited digital literacy. For the Federal Government, the zero-rating policy is therefore expected to give digital learning a wider reach, particularly among learners in underserved and hard-to-reach communities where conventional educational infrastructure remains inadequate. Alausa said poverty and geography must no longer determine the educational opportunities available to Nigerian children, arguing that a mobile phone, tablet or computer could effectively become a classroom, library and gateway to opportunities if the financial barrier to accessing educational content was removed. He said the initiative formed part of the digital transformation component of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, being implemented through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative. The minister explained that the Federal Ministry of Education was simultaneously strengthening the infrastructure required to manage a modern education system through initiatives such as the Nigeria Education Data Infrastructure, Digital Nigeria Education Management Information System and Learner Identification Number. However, he stressed that the success of the government’s digital reforms would not be determined by the number of platforms created or devices deployed, but by whether the interventions actually reached learners and improved educational outcomes. “The real measure of digital transformation would be its ability to reach the learner and improve the quality of education,” he said. Nigeria has previously experimented with zero-rated educational platforms, including the Nigeria Learning Passport, developed by the Federal Government, UNICEF and other partners to provide curriculum content to learners and teachers. UNICEF had reported that data charges were removed for users accessing the Nigeria Learning Passport through whitelisting on an Airtel SIM, while connectivity was also extended to schools in hard-to-reach communities. The latest initiative, however, signals a broader attempt by the Federal Government to institutionalise zero-rated access to approved educational platforms as digital technology increasingly becomes an important component of teaching and learning. While the government seeks to throw open the doors of digital education, Alausa said it was equally concerned about the risks children face in the online environment. He disclosed that plans were underway for regulated internet access for every child below 16 years, citing growing concerns over cyberattacks and other threats associated with children’s increasing exposure to digital platforms. “At some point, there would be regulated internet access for every child below the age of 16 years as part of measures to strengthen online child protection,” the minister said. The proposed regulation introduces a new dimension to the government’s digital education strategy, suggesting that greater access to technology must be accompanied by stronger safeguards for children. Alausa called for sustained collaboration between the Federal Ministry of Education, state governments, the Nigerian Communications Commission, telecommunications operators, technology companies, development partners, educational institutions and teachers to ensure the success of the initiative. He also challenged stakeholders to ensure that Nigeria’s digital education drive produced more than technology consumers, saying the country must raise a generation capable of creating technology, innovating and using digital tools to solve societal problems. The post FG scraps data charges for students appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: C’River elders back Gov Otu
items.description: —Governor vows to pay second gratuity tranche before December By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR The Cross River State Elders’ Forum has endorsed Governor Bassey Edet Otu for a second term, citing his administration’s strides in security, healthcare and infrastructure. The governor, meanwhile, has announced plans to release the next tranche of retirees’ gratuities before December, assuring pensioners of his administration’s continued commitment to clearing the backlog. The endorsement was contained in an address by the Forum’s Chairman, Col. Pam Ogar (retd.), former Military Administrator of Kwara State, during a courtesy visit to the governor at the State Executive Council Chamber, Calabar, on Thursday. Ogar said the Forum’s decision followed a careful review of the administration’s performance. “The Forum hereby expresses its confidence in your administration and accordingly, wholeheartedly encourages you to present yourself for a second term in office,” he declared. He said a second tenure would enable Otu to consolidate the gains recorded by his administration, complete ongoing developmental programmes and pursue uncompleted projects initiated by his predecessor. The elders commended the governor’s “People First” philosophy, citing the Cross River State Public Complaints Office and the Cross River State Live platform as evidence of his administration’s responsiveness to citizens. They also lauded reforms in the health sector, particularly the upgrade of nursing schools to Colleges of Nursing in Obudu, Ogoja, Itigidi and Calabar. On security, the Forum praised efforts to curb robbery and kidnapping but urged the government to intensify action against cattle grazers, illegal settlements and iron scavengers in Obanliku, Obudu, Ogoja, Ikom and Obubra. The elders, however, appealed to the governor to expedite the payment of outstanding gratuities and pensions. “It is our passionate appeal that government take a serious look into this problem to ameliorate the sufferings of retirees,” Ogar said. He also urged the governor to prioritise industrialisation during a second term, saying Cross River must move beyond consumption to production, value addition, job creation and sustainable economic growth. Responding, Otu described the elders’ visit and counsel as invaluable, noting their wealth of experience in different professions and their contributions to nation and state building. “When I look at the faces here, I see people who have reached the peak in their different professions and who have had experiences which we still need in terms of nation-building and state-building,” he said. On retirees’ benefits, Otu disclosed that the government had commenced arrangements to release the next tranche of gratuity before December, assuring pensioners that efforts to clear the backlog would continue. The governor also addressed the state’s efforts to reclaim its oil-producing assets, stressing the need to preserve the resources for future generations. “These things were created by God and the universe. We take care of it and then hand it over to the next generation,” he said. The post 2027: C’River elders back Gov Otu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé, ce jeudi, 10 septembre 2026, à Bobo, l’hebdomadaire Conseil des ministres. Selon le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, le Conseil a examiné plusieurs dossiers et pris d'importantes décisions pour la bonne marche de la Nation et pour le plein épanouissement des Burkinabè, conformément à la vision de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Pour le compte du Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant adoption du guide méthodologique de description des postes de travail dans l'administration publique. Selon le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ, il s'agit d'une mise à jour qui permet de prendre en compte des emplois de gestionnaires scolaires et universitaires et l'administration des affaires économiques. « Le nouveau guide qui vient d'être adopté s'applique aux collectivités territoriales, aux établissements publics de l'État, aux sociétés d'État, aux sociétés d'économie mixte et aussi aux autorités administratives indépendantes », a expliqué le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple. Il a noté que ce guide permet de prendre en compte la notion de profil idéal, et pour l'occupation d’un poste défini, de tenir compte des profils disposant de compétences similaires dans les cas de la prise en compte équitable de tous les emplois. Pour le compte du Ministère de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Conseil a adopté un rapport autorisant le financement d'initiatives sectorielles d'accroissement de la capacité énergétique du Burkina Faso. Selon le Ministre Yacouba Zabré GOUBA, ce projet, d'un montant de plus de 104 milliards FCFA, va permettre de renforcer les capacités opérationnelles de la SONABEL et de la nouvelle Agence Faso Vêenem afin d’atteindre un taux d'électrification de 70% à l'horizon 2030 et réduire notre dépendance énergétique. « Il s'agira également, de mettre à la disposition de la Société nationale d’électricité et de l'Agence Faso Vêenem des équipements et des infrastructures nécessaires pour leur permettre d’assurer l'extension des réseaux de transport et de distribution », a indiqué le Ministre GOUBA. items.title: Mahama charges new Supreme Court justices to protect judicial independence
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged three newly sworn-in Justices of the Supreme Court to uphold the Constitution, protect judicial independence and ensure that their decisions strengthen public confidence in Ghana’s justice system. Speaking at the swearing-in ceremony at Jubilee House on Thursday, September 10, President Mahama congratulated Justice Sophia Rosetta Oduokouan Bernasko-Essah, Justice Edward Amoako Asante and Anthony Fawson Jr, popularly known as Tony Fawson, following Parliament’s approval of their appointments. He described membership of the Supreme Court as one of the highest and most demanding responsibilities in Ghana’s constitutional democracy, noting that the Court’s authority ultimately depended on the confidence and trust of the Ghanaian people. “The authority of the Court does not rest on force or political power. It rests on the confidence and trust of the people,” the President said, stressing that cases must be determined independently, impartially and strictly according to law. President Mahama said the three new justices brought complementary experience that would strengthen the country’s highest court. Justice Bernasko-Essah, whose career includes service on the Court of Appeal, was commended for her extensive judicial experience and understanding of the practical administration of justice. The President said her elevation reflected her competence, discipline and dedication, while urging her to contribute to the clarity, consistency and development of Ghanaian jurisprudence. Justice Asante was praised for combining national judicial experience with regional expertise gained from his tenure as President of the ECOWAS Court of Justice. According to Mr Mahama, his exposure to issues including regional integration, treaty obligations, human rights and the relationship between domestic and international law would bring an important perspective to the Supreme Court. Mr Fawson, who joins the bench from private legal practice and previously served as President of the Ghana Bar Association, was described as bringing decades of practical experience from the legal profession. The President noted that his transition from advocacy to adjudication would require a fundamental shift in responsibility, with the judge required to rise above competing interests and determine cases on the basis of law, evidence and justice. President Mahama reaffirmed his commitment to judicial independence, describing it not as a privilege for judges but as a safeguard for citizens whose rights may depend on impartial decisions, particularly in politically sensitive or difficult cases. He, however, stressed that independence must be accompanied by accountability, discipline and fidelity to the judicial oath. “The oath you are taking today is consequential, not ceremonial,” he said, reminding the justices of their obligation to administer justice without fear, favour, affection or ill will, and to defend the Constitution. He also called on the judiciary to address delays in the administration of justice, warning that prolonged cases, avoidable adjournments and delays in delivering judgments could undermine public confidence and amount to a denial of justice. The President urged the judiciary to continue reforms aimed at improving efficiency and accessibility, including the appropriate use of technology. He said justice must be accessible to all Ghanaians regardless of income, social status or geographical location, adding that the effectiveness of the judicial system should ultimately be measured by how fairly and promptly citizens can obtain justice. President Mahama said the three new justices had assumed office at a time when the Supreme Court’s role remained critical to the protection of constitutional rights, preservation of the separation of powers and enforcement of the principle that no individual or institution is above the law. He expressed confidence that their combined judicial, regional and private-practice experience would deepen the Court’s deliberations and contribute to the continued development of Ghana’s legal and constitutional order.

items.title: Mahama swears in three new Supreme Court justices
items.description: President John Mahama has sworn in three new justices to the Supreme Court, urging them to uphold the Constitution, protect the rights of citizens, and ensure that no individual or institution is placed above the law. The new justices are Justice Sophia Rosetta Bernasko Essah, Justice Edward Amoako Asante, and private legal practitioner Anthony Forson Jnr. Speaking at the swearing-in ceremony on Thursday, September 10, at the Jubilee House, President Mahama said the Supreme Court holds a critical position in Ghana’s democratic system as the country’s final judicial authority. “The Supreme Court occupies a unique and indispensable place in governing our Republic,” he said. He said that decisions of the Court have far-reaching consequences, from interpreting the Constitution to resolving matters of national importance and shaping the development of Ghana’s laws. “As the final judicial authority, its decisions give meaning to our Constitution, settle questions of profound national importance and shape the evolution of our laws,” President Mahama said. The President said the authority of the Supreme Court should not come from political influence or force but from the confidence Ghanaians have in its ability to deliver justice independently and fairly. “The authority of the Court does not rest on force or political power. It rests on the confidence and trust of the people,” he said. According to him, citizens must be assured that cases brought before the Court will be determined without political or other external influence. “Confidence and trust that every matter brought before it will be determined independently, impartially and strictly according to the law,” he said. President Mahama said membership of the Supreme Court therefore requires more than legal expertise. “Those appointed to the Supreme Court must therefore possess more than just legal knowledge.” “They must demonstrate sound judgment, personal integrity, intellectual courage, patience and a deep commitment to justice,” he added.

items.title: Kaduna attack: No one has monopoly on violence — ADC warns
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has warned that no one has a monopoly on violence, following an attack on its members in Kaduna State, saying those introducing thuggery into the 2027 political process are playing a dangerous game. The party said the attack was an unacceptable escalation at a time when political activities ahead of the 2027 elections were only beginning, warning that violence must not be allowed to become an instrument of political competition. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said its commitment to peaceful democratic participation should not be mistaken for weakness. “Let nobody mistake our commitment to peaceful democratic participation for weakness. No political party has a monopoly on non-state sanctioned violence. Once violence becomes an accepted instrument of political competition, nobody can predict where it ends,” Abdullahi said. The party urged security agencies to immediately identify those responsible for the attack, including anyone who sponsored or organised it, and bring them to justice. “This is why the security agencies must act now. Those responsible for the attack, as well as anyone who sponsored or organised it, must be identified, arrested and prosecuted,” the ADC said. The party also expressed solidarity with its governorship candidate, Hon. Isa Ashiru, and other members affected by the incident, while calling on the Kaduna State Government to guarantee the safety of opposition parties. “Kaduna belongs to its people, not to any party,” the ADC said, warning against any attempt to use intimidation to push it out of the political arena. “If anyone believes intimidation will frighten the ADC off the political field, they have badly miscalculated,” Abdullahi said. The ADC said it would continue to organise and campaign across Kaduna State despite the attack, insisting that the 2027 election must be determined by political ideas and the ballot box. “We will not be intimidated. We will organise, we will campaign, and we will compete in every part of Kaduna State. The 2027 elections must be decided by ideas competing at the ballot box, not by thugs and bruises,” the party said. items.title: La Liga: Rodri apologises after describing Valencia as ‘very weak’
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona midfielder Rodri has apologised to Valencia after television footage appeared to show him describing the La Liga side as “very weak”. According to the BBC, Rodri allegedly made the comments to Barcelona teammates Pau Cubarsí and Raphinha while sitting on the bench after being substituted during Sunday’s 5-0 win at Mestalla. The footage has no audio, but Spanish broadcaster Movistar said it had lip-read Rodri as saying, “They’re really weak. They haven’t got past the halfway line.” The comments sparked criticism from Valencia fans and sections of the Spanish media, with Rodri accused of disrespecting the struggling club. Rodri, however, said he had apologised to Valencia captain and Spain teammate José Gayà as well as the entire squad. “I also want to make it clear that it was simply an expression of surprise,” Rodri said after Barcelona’s 5-1 Champions League victory over Feyenoord on Wednesday. “At no point did I intend to mock anyone or take a difficult moment for a team out of context.” Rodri said his comments were made during a private conversation and had been taken out of context. “But at no point did I mean any disrespect. My apologies to Valencia,” he added. Valencia are bottom of La Liga after failing to win any of their opening four matches, while Barcelona have made a perfect start to the campaign. Rodri joined Barcelona this summer in a £65 million move from Manchester City after helping Spain win the 2026 World Cup, where he was named the tournament’s Golden Ball winner. items.title: US delivers military equipment to Nigeria
items.description: —Support targets counterterrorism operations The United States has delivered military equipment to the Nigerian Air Force in Lagos and Kainji, Niger State, to support counterterrorism operations. The US Africa Command (AFRICOM), in a statement on its website on Thursday, said the equipment was delivered in September through a US Air Force C-17 aircraft. According to the command, the delivery was part of a foreign military sales agreement between the United States and Nigerian militaries. “The delivery furthers the strategic partnership between the two nations in order to enhance Nigerian-led efforts to counter terrorism in the region. U.S. military support to the Armed Forces of Nigeria is by its invitation and rooted in respect for Nigerian sovereignty,” AFRICOM said. The development comes weeks after the AFRICOM Commander, Gen. Dagvin Anderson, announced a reduction in the number of US troops deployed to Nigeria following a May operation that killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, identified by US officials as the second-in-command of ISIS, in the Lake Chad Basin. American and Nigerian officials had described the relatively small US deployment in Nigeria as having produced significant results. However, small teams of US trainers and intelligence analysts are expected to remain in Nigeria after the larger contingent is withdrawn by late September. The report also quoted American officials as describing the deployment in Nigeria as a potential model for future US counterterrorism operations in Africa. The post US delivers military equipment to Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Boulgou : Natingba Kissous Ouédraogo prend la tête du Collège d’enseignement général de Zoaga
items.description: BURKINA-INSTALLATION-DIRECTION-COLLEGE-COMMUNE-ZOAGA Boulgou : Natingba Kissous Ouédraogo prend la tête du Collège d’enseignement général de Zoaga Zoaga, 03 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le nouveau directeur du Collège d’enseignement général (CEG) de Zoaga, Natingba Kissous Ouédraogo, a été installé dans ses fonctions le mercredi 03 septembre 2026, en remplacement de Jean Marie Bouda. La cérémonie de passation de charges a été présidée par le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Zoaga, Bernard Yaméogo, dans la salle des fêtes de la mairie. Elle s’est déroulée en présence du représentant de la Direction provinciale de l’Enseignement post-primaire et secondaire du Boulgou, des directeurs des CEG de Bougré et de Zabré, du proviseur du lycée de Bissaya ainsi que du corps enseignant du collège de Zoaga. Le camarade Yaméogo a procédé à l’installation officielle du directeur entrant, Natingba Kissous Ouédraogo. Il succède ainsi à Jean Marie Bouda qui a passé plus de cinq ans à la tête de l’établissement. Dans son allocution, le PDS a souhaité la bienvenue aux participants, soulignant que leur présence témoigne de l’intérêt accordé au secteur de l’éducation dans la commune. Il a félicité le nouveau responsable de l’école pour sa nomination et l’a invité à faire preuve d’abnégation et de persévérance pour le succès des élèves. « Je vous souhaite une fructueuse mission dans notre chère commune de Zoaga », a-t-il conclu. Prenant la parole, le directeur nouvellement installé s’est engagé à travailler avec rigueur, transparence et dans un esprit de bonne collaboration. Il a sollicité le soutien de l’ensemble de ses collaborateurs pour la réussite de son mandat. Située à une dizaine de kilomètres de la frontière du Ghana, la commune de Zoaga relève de la province du Boulgou, région du Nakambé. Agence d’Information du Burkina YL/sm/ata/zs

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Mouvement sunnite inaugure l’Université Privée An-Nahdah d’Afrique à Ouagadougou
items.description: L’Université Privée An-Nahdah d’Afrique (UP-2A) a officiellement ouvert ses portes, ce 10 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Cette université, présentée comme un joyau du Mouvement sunnite du Burkina Faso (MSBF), dispose d’infrastructures académiques modernes et d’une offre de formation destinée à accueillir les étudiants dès la rentrée académique 2026-2027. Située dans le quartier Karpala, derrière le Tribunal de grande instance Ouaga II (TGI Ouaga II), l’Université Privée An-Nahdah d’Afrique s’étend sur une superficie de plus de 28 500 m². Elle compte cinq bâtiments, dont deux principaux. Ces derniers abritent 28 salles de cours, deux amphithéâtres, un laboratoire, deux bibliothèques, dont l’une physique et l’autre virtuelle, ainsi que diverses infrastructures annexes. Grâce à ces infrastructures, l’établissement est en mesure d’accueillir jusqu’à 1 680 étudiants. Pour favoriser de bonnes conditions d’apprentissage, l’université dispose également d’une infirmerie et d’une grande salle informatique. Pour cette première rentrée, l’UP-2A propose deux grandes filières, chacune subdivisée en deux options. La filière Sciences juridiques, politiques et de l’administration comprend ainsi les options Droit public et Droit privé. La filière Sciences économiques et de gestion propose, quant à elle, les options Marketing et Communication ainsi que Logistique internationale. A travers cette initiative, le MSBF s’inscrit en droite ligne dans la vision du président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré -©️Faso7 Avec ces infrastructures et cette offre de formation, l’UP-2A entend se positionner comme un nouvel acteur de l’enseignement supérieur privé au Burkina Faso, à l’occasion de la rentrée académique 2026-2027. Selon Oumarou Zoungrana, président du MSBF, cette initiative s’inscrit dans la vision portée par le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, en faveur d’une éducation de qualité et accessible à tous. L’investissement initial consacré au projet est estimé à environ 1,5 milliard de F CFA. À terme, les différents projets d’extension devraient porter l’engagement financier global à près de 3 milliards de F CFA. Pour le président du MSBF, l’éducation constitue un véritable outil de développement, d’émancipation et de transformation de la société, mais également un levier de souveraineté. « Nous voulons contribuer à former des citoyens compétents et responsables, capables d’entreprendre, de créer de la richesse, de servir leur communauté, attachés à leur patrie, respectueux des autres. Nous voulons donc que l’UP-2A contribue à former des femmes et des hommes capables de participer à la cohésion de notre Nation » , a-t-il souligné. Les installatiions sont effectués de manière à assurer le confort aux futurs étudiants -©Faso7 Prenant la parole au nom de la directrice régionale en charge de l’Enseignement supérieur, Dr Oumar Lingani a félicité le Mouvement sunnite du Burkina Faso pour cette initiative et lui a exprimé sa reconnaissance. Selon lui, l’ouverture de l’UP-2A contribue au renforcement de l’offre de formation et à la formation d’une jeunesse compétente, consciente et engagée au service de la Nation. Dr Oumar Lingani a, par ailleurs, encouragé l’UP-2A à faire de l’excellence, de la discipline, de l’innovation, de l’éthique et de l’engagement patriotique les piliers de sa mission. « Cette université vient contribuer au renforcement de l’offre de formation et à la construction d’une jeunesse compétente, consciente et engagée au service de cette nation », a-t-il indiqué. À travers l’UP-2A, le Mouvement sunnite du Burkina Faso entend ainsi apporter sa contribution à la dynamique nationale en matière d’éducation. L’association ambitionne notamment de participer à l’élargissement de l’offre de formation et au renforcement des compétences de la jeunesse burkinabè. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le Mouvement sunnite inaugure l’Université Privée An-Nahdah d’Afrique à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Gestion des carrières au Burkina Faso : Le gouvernement adopte un nouveau guide méthodologique de description des postes
items.description: Réuni en Conseil des ministres ce jeudi 10 septembre 2026 sous la présidence du Chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le gouvernement a franchi une étape importante dans la modernisation de la fonction publique. Sur rapport du Ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, l'exécutif a adopté un décret portant adoption du guide méthodologique de description des postes de travail dans l'administration publique. Cet outil rénové s'applique à l'ensemble des structures publiques et parapubliques afin d'intégrer de nouveaux emplois sectoriels et d'instaurer une gestion plus équitable des compétences basée sur la notion de « profil idéal ». La réorganisation de l'appareil administratif se poursuit conformément à la vision de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). À l'issue du Conseil des ministres du 10 septembre 2026 tenu à Bobo-Dioulasso, le gouvernement a validé la mise à jour du guide méthodologique de description des postes de travail. Présentée par le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias Traoré, cette réforme vise à ajuster les instruments de gestion des ressources humaines aux réalités actuelles du service public. La nouvelle mouture permet notamment de formaliser et de prendre en compte les emplois de gestionnaires scolaires et universitaires, ainsi que ceux de l'administration des affaires économiques. Un champ d'application élargi à l'ensemble du secteur public L'une des innovations majeures de ce texte réside dans l'étendue de son périmètre juridique et opérationnel. Comme l'a précisé le ministre Mathias Traoré, les dispositions du nouveau guide ne se limitent pas à l'administration centrale : elles s'imposent désormais aux collectivités territoriales, aux établissements publics de l'État, aux sociétés d'État, aux sociétés d'économie mixte ainsi qu'aux autorités administratives indépendantes. Cette harmonisation garantit une cartographie homogène des fonctions et des responsabilités sur toute l'étendue du territoire national. Vers une occupation équitable des postes fondée sur le « profil idéal » Au-delà de la simple codification des tâches, la réforme introduit le concept de « profil idéal » pour l'attribution des responsabilités. Selon les explications fournies par le département des Serviteurs du Peuple, cette approche permet de prendre en compte, lors de la pourvue d'un poste défini, les candidats disposant de compétences similaires. L'objectif affiché est d'assurer un traitement équitable de tous les emplois tout en veillant à l'adéquation exacte entre les exigences du poste et les capacités de l'agent. L’article Gestion des carrières au Burkina Faso : Le gouvernement adopte un nouveau guide méthodologique de description des postes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Trump administration proposes waiving grace period for H-1B holders after job loss
items.description: The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday. Under the planned rule change, published in the Federal Register by the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), those with H-1B and certain other temporary work visas would have to leave the country as soon as their employment ends — a potential blow to top American tech companies that rely heavily on foreign workers. It is the latest step by US President Donald Trump to limit legal migration since returning to office in January 2025. His administration has also introduced higher visa fees for skilled workers and recently paused immigrant visa appointments at US missions around the world while it implements a new training programme. Companies impacted by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead. In some situations, immigrant workers who leave could potentially reapply if their employer petitions for them, it added. “DHS presumes that they will either offer the same jobs to equally qualified US workers or go through the I-129 petition process depending on their workforce requirement,” the notice said. The 60-day grace period, in place since 2017, allows foreign workers time to find another US job or get their affairs in order, whether selling a home or pulling children out of school before leaving the country. H-1B visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking talent from India and China, allowing them to fill roles where there is sometimes a lack of qualified US workers. Consultancy companies such as Deloitte, PwC and Ernst and Young, as well as outsourcing giants like Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCL Tech and LTIMindtree, are top H-1B sponsors. Lawyers for Berardi Immigration Law, which specialises in business-related immigration issues, said the move would “sharply compress the timeline HR teams have to manage layoffs and offboarding for foreign national employees”. If implemented, the change would also apply to E-1 international trader visa holders; E-2 commercial vehicle operator visa holders; L-1 short-term work for executives or managers with international companies; O-1 visas for people “with an extraordinary ability” in science, sports or the arts; and TN professional workers. It would also impact H-1B1 skilled worker visa holders from Singapore and Chile and E-3 speciality worker visa holders from Australia. The rule is subject to a two-month public comment period before it can be enacted into law.

items.title: LHC moved against PMDC's directives for repatriation of Afghan students
items.description: LAHORE: Thirteen Afghan medical students on Thursday filed multiple petitions before the Lahore High Court (LHC), challenging directives from the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) that ordered their return to Afghanistan. The petitioners, comprising seven women and six men, filed the petitions through Advocate Asad Jamal. They were enrolled at different institutions in Lahore, including King Edward Medical University, Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical & Dental College and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences. The petitioners said they were removed from their colleges on PMDC’s instructions, with the council acting as the top regulatory body under the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council Act 2023 . They argued that PMDC and the medical colleges lacked the legal authority to expel the students. The petitioners argued that PMDC’s powers must be exercised within the bounds of the Constitution and Pakistan’s international legal obligations, and that neither the 2023 Act nor constitutional or international principles permitted the council to act arbitrarily, particularly against students who had already invested years in their medical education in Lahore and across Punjab. Many of the petitioners hold scholarships under the Higher Education Commission (HEC)-sponsored Allama Iqbal Scholarship programme . The HEC, in July 2025, held a reception to welcome around 350 Afghan students arriving in Pakistan to pursue their studies. Nilofar Nikzad, one of the petitioners, said she had completed two years of medical studies in Afghanistan before being forced to abandon her education there because of Taliban restrictions on women’s access to education. The petitioners said the sudden and disruptive process led to their evictions from hostels by their respective colleges and left them without accommodation as their academic futures hung in the balance. They said the PMDC’s directives had caused significant distress among Afghan medical students studying across Pakistan, prompting them to seek recourse from the courts as a last resort. The petitioners requested the LHC to decide on two PMDC directives, issued on July 31 and September 1, and declare them “illegal and unconstitutional”, without lawful authority and void from inception. “The impugned orders are discriminatory against women and all other Afghan students present in Pakistan,” one of the petitions claimed. The petitions have been fixed for hearing before Justice Khalid Ishaq on Friday. PMDC order On September 1, PMDC issued a notification directing Afghan medical students enrolled in Pakistani colleges “to return to Afghanistan”. The notification also barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session. Soon after, reports circulated on social media about the alleged expulsion of Afghan nationals who were studying at public sector medical colleges in Lahore. According to a health ministry official, an “in principle” decision had been made to send Afghan students enrolled in Pakistani medical universities back to their country, due to the ongoing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul. When asked about the reported expulsion of Afghan students, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan had told Dawn that “any foreign national without a valid visa and passport” was liable to deportation under the Illegal Foreigner Repatriation Plan (IFRP). Jamal, the petitioners’ counsel, claimed in a post on X that there was “no distinction made between valid visa and invalid stay by PMDC in its directives”. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has condemned the PMDC decision, warning that the move could turn an education policy into a humanitarian crisis. It said around 100 Afghan medical and dental students in Lahore alone could be affected, including an estimated 20 to 40 women.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Un plan massif de 104 milliards FCFA pour atteindre 70% de taux d’électrification
items.description: Pour répondre au défi de l'accès universel à l'électricité et soutenir le développement économique du pays, le Conseil des ministres du 10 septembre 2026 a approuvé un rapport déterminant du Ministère de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières. L'exécutif a autorisé le financement d'initiatives sectorielles d'un montant de plus de 104 milliards FCFA destinées à renforcer les capacités énergétiques nationales. Ce projet d'envergure vise à équiper la SONABEL ainsi que la nouvelle Agence Faso Vêenem afin de porter le taux d'électrification du Burkina Faso à 70% à l'horizon 2030 tout en réduisant la dépendance énergétique extérieure. Face à la croissance continue de la demande en électricité, l'État passe à l'offensive. Lors de la séance hebdomadaire du Conseil des ministres présidée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré à Bobo-Dioulasso, le gouvernement a donné son vert pour la mobilisation de plus de 104 milliards FCFA. Porté par le Ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, le Camarade Yacouba Zabré Gouba, ce programme financier permettra d'acquérir les équipements industriels et de réaliser les infrastructures nécessaires à l'extension des réseaux de transport et de distribution de courant électrique. Cet investissement historique bénéficiera en premier lieu aux deux bras armés de l'État en matière d'électricité : la Société nationale d'électricité du Burkina (SONABEL) et la toute nouvelle Agence Faso Vêenem. Le renforcement de leurs capacités opérationnelles doit leur permettre de déployer des réseaux plus solides et mieux maillés à travers les régions du pays, garantissant ainsi une fourniture d'énergie plus stable et mieux répartie. L'ambition stratégique affichée par le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba est claire : faire passer le taux d'électrification national à 70% d'ici 2030. En augmentant l'offre locale et en modernisant les maillons de distribution, le gouvernement entend assumer la pleine souveraineté énergétique du territoire national et réduire de manière drastique la dépendance du pays vis-à-vis des importations d'électricité. items.title: At least 14 children killed in DR Congo school fire stampede
items.description: A stampede after a fire broke out in a school in the eastern DR Congo city of Bukavu has killed at least 14 children, local and health sources said on Thursday. A blaze of “unknown” origins began near a school in the Bagira district on the city’s northern outskirts early on Thursday “while the children were in the middle of class”, local leader Patrice Buduge told AFP. “This was followed by a violent stampede that forced students to trample over one another or look for a dangerous way out; many of them fainted and others lost consciousness,” he said. He said the provisional toll was “more than 500 homes burned and 27 deaths”. AFP was not able to independently verify the toll with other official sources. “We received around 50 students, including several teachers, in a critical state of asphyxia,” said Christophe Zigashane, a nurse in a neighbouring clinic. “Among them, 10 were dead and four others died at the scene. That makes a total of 14 deaths, all under 10 years old,” he said. He said that 27 people including two teachers had been transferred in a critical state to other hospitals in the city. Large columns of smoke were still visible around the site of the fire at midday on Thursday, an AFP correspondent saw. The fire devastated a wide, densely built area on a hillside where residents were making their way through the debris of charred houses, strewn with crumpled sheets of metal. Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu province, is controlled by the M23 anti-governmental group, which has seized large swathes of eastern DRC. The city lies on the shores of Lake Kivu and is known for its wooden plank houses built on hillsides. AFP The post At least 14 children killed in DR Congo school fire stampede appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: TUC calls for urgent review of Labour Act to strengthen workers’ rights
items.description: The Trades Union Congress (TUC) has called for an urgent review of Ghana’s Labour Act to strengthen workers’ rights and address concerns over low wages, inadequate pension benefits, rising living costs, and insecure employment. TUC’s Secretary-General, Joshua Ansah, made the call while addressing the press on Thursday, September 10. He said low pay remains one of the most urgent concerns confronting workers, with wages for many households failing to keep pace with the cost of food, rent, transport, utilities, education, and healthcare. “Low pay is one of the most urgent concerns confronting workers,” Mr Ansah said. He also raised concerns about pension benefits, saying many retirees receive benefits that are too low to meet their basic needs, particularly medical care. “A pension should protect dignity in old age. Yet, many retirees receive benefits that are too low to meet basic needs, particularly medical care,” he said. According to him, high and rising living costs are further eroding the real value of pensions, while the effective pension growth rate for workers in the informal economy remains too low. Mr Ansah further expressed concern about workers performing continuous core duties under what he described as “so-called short-term contracts.” He said some were engaged through labour contractors or arrangements that denied them equal treatment, job security, social security and access to a union. “The law should look at the reality of their employment relationship, not merely the level placed on their contract,” he said. The TUC supports a review of the Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651), saying Ghana needs a modern law that responds to changing forms of work, strengthens labour institutions and advances decent work. The Congress therefore called for an urgent and comprehensive review of Ghana’s labour laws to ensure they adequately protect workers, address emerging forms of employment, strengthen social protection, and promote decent work.

items.title: Législatives 2026 : 7.288 candidats et 1.850 listes en lice
items.description: Le ministère de l’Intérieur a dévoilé ce jeudi les chiffres définitifs des candidatures aux élections législatives du 23 septembre 2026. Au total, 7.288 candidats et candidates se présentent à ce scrutin, répartis sur 1.850 listes, soit une moyenne nationale de plus de 18 candidatures pour chaque siège de la Chambre des représentants. La période de dépôt des candidatures s’est achevée mercredi 9 septembre dans des conditions qualifiées de normales par le ministère, qui fait également état d’une participation en hausse par rapport aux précédentes élections législatives comparables. Au total, 28 formations politiques, dont une alliance constituée spécialement pour ces élections, prennent part à cette échéance. Dans les circonscriptions locales, le ministère recense 1.615 listes, regroupant 5.505 candidats et candidates. En 2021, ces circonscriptions avaient enregistré 1.472 listes et 5.046 candidatures. Pour les circonscriptions régionales, réservées aux femmes, 235 listes ont été déposées, avec 1.783 candidates, soit près de 20 candidatures par siège. Plus de 2.600 candidatures féminines La participation des femmes représente l’un des chiffres marquants communiqués par le ministère. Elles sont au total 2.658 candidates, soit 36,47% de l’ensemble des candidatures. Ce chiffre comprend les 1.783 candidates engagées dans les circonscriptions régionales et 875 candidates dans les circonscriptions locales. Le ministère relève également que 121 listes locales sont conduites par des femmes. Le scrutin verra par ailleurs la participation de 227 membres du Parlement en exercice, dont 204 députés, 20 députées et trois conseillers. À côté des formations politiques, deux listes de candidats sans affiliation partisane ont également été déposées dans deux circonscriptions locales. Les principaux partis présents dans les circonscriptions Les chiffres du ministère montrent une présence particulièrement large des principales formations politiques. Le Parti de l’authenticité et de la modernité (PAM), le Parti de l’Istiqlal, le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS) et le Parti de la justice et du développement (PJD) présentent chacun 92 listes locales, soit 305 candidats, auxquelles s’ajoutent 12 listes régionales comprenant 90 candidates. Le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) compte également 92 listes locales et 305 candidats, avec 11 listes régionales regroupant 80 candidates. L’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) présente 90 listes locales et 301 candidats, ainsi que 11 listes régionales et 87 candidates. Le Mouvement populaire compte, lui, 86 listes locales et 290 candidats, et 12 listes régionales avec 90 candidates. Le reste des formations engagées dans la course présente des niveaux de couverture variables, allant de plusieurs dizaines de listes locales à des implantations plus limitées. Avec la clôture du dépôt des candidatures, la compétition entre désormais dans sa phase de campagne. Les 28 formations engagées disposent jusqu’au 22 septembre à minuit pour mobiliser les électeurs, avant le scrutin du 23 septembre 2026. items.title: AMA proposes city-to-city partnerships with Russian cities
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) and the Embassy of the Russian Federation in Ghana have begun exploring new areas of cooperation aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and promoting practical development partnerships. The areas identified include education, investment, urban development, culture and people-to-people exchanges. The discussions took place on Monday, September 7, 2026, when the Russian Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Andrei Ordash, paid a courtesy call on the Mayor of Accra, Hon. Michael Kpakpo Allotey. The meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to discuss areas where Accra and Russian cities could collaborate to promote knowledge sharing, institutional development and economic opportunities. Mayor Allotey said Accra had much to learn from the development experiences of Russian cities, particularly in urban planning, infrastructure development, technology and metropolitan administration. He expressed optimism that the city could adopt relevant best practices from Russian cities while also sharing its own experiences in local governance and city management. The Mayor specifically highlighted Moscow as a city from which Accra could draw valuable lessons in managing the challenges associated with rapid urbanisation and metropolitan growth. He subsequently proposed the establishment of city-to-city partnerships between Accra and selected Russian cities. According to him, such partnerships would provide a structured platform for knowledge exchange, institutional collaboration and development cooperation. The proposed collaboration is expected to create opportunities for technical exchanges and joint initiatives in areas of mutual interest, while strengthening relations between institutions and communities in Ghana and Russia. The meeting forms part of efforts by the AMA to expand international partnerships that can contribute to Accra’s development and improve the delivery of services to residents. Both sides expressed their commitment to pursuing the discussions and identifying practical areas where cooperation could translate into tangible benefits for Accra and its people.

items.title: Arsenal close to finalising Arteta’s new contract — reports
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal are close to finalising a new long-term contract for manager Mikel Arteta, with talks between the club and the Spaniard progressing positively. According to the BBC, discussions have advanced in recent weeks, with all parties confident that Arteta will sign a new deal and remain in charge at the Emirates Stadium. Arteta, whose current contract has nine months remaining, is expected to become one of the highest-paid managers in world football under the improved terms. His existing deal is worth £10m a season, with a further £5m available if Arsenal qualify for the Champions League, but the club are committed to significantly improving his package. Arteta has already made clear that he wants to remain at Arsenal, saying last month that he was “very happy” at the club and that the timing of his new contract would not be an issue. Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick has also described the agreement as a “matter of time”. Since taking charge in December 2019, Arteta has transformed Arsenal into Premier League champions after the club’s 22-year wait for the title and has established himself as the longest-serving manager in English football. The Spaniard has also become a central figure in Arsenal’s transfer strategy, with the club’s recruitment and pursuit of elite players closely aligned with his vision. The summer arrivals of Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, as well as Arsenal’s unsuccessful pursuits of Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, reflected the club’s willingness to invest heavily in the squad. The BBC reports that Arsenal’s ownership sees Arteta’s continued presence as central to the club’s ambitions, particularly with the current squad considered capable of building a sustained legacy. A new agreement would take Arteta closer to a decade in charge of Arsenal, where he has already surpassed every other current Premier League and EFL manager in length of service. items.title: Sétif : chute mortelle d’un ado de 15 ans dans un puits de 30 m
items.description: Nouveau drame en Algérie lié à la chute d’un enfant dans un puits. Après la tragédie d’El Bayadh qui a emporté le petit Ayoub, 10 ans, un adolescent de 15 ans a trouvé la mort à Sétif dans des circonstances semblables. La Protection civile a annoncé ce jeudi 10 septembre que le corps sans vie d’un enfant a été repêché dans un puits à El Eulma. L'intervention a eu lieu dans la matinée vers 9h afin de sauver l’enfant qui a fait une chute dans un puits de 30 mètres au village de Zaouia, dans la commune de Barez, daïra d'El Eulma (Sétif). Une ambulance et un camion de secours ont été mobilisés pour cette opération. Malgré les efforts, l’adolescent de 15 ans n’a pas pu être sauvé. Les éléments de la Protection civile ont repêché le corps sans vie qui a été transféré à la morgue de l’hôpital local. Deux enfants meurent dans un puits en moins d’une semaine Samedi 5 septembre, toute l’Algérie a été bouleversée par l’annonce du décès du petit Ayoub, 10 ans, après une chute dans un puits artésien de 80 mètres dans la wilaya d’El Bayadh. L’enfant était coincé au fond du puits depuis mercredi 2 septembre. Malgré les efforts colossaux de la Protection civile et des autorités locales, le garçon n’a pas pu être sauvé. Immédiatement après, des opérations de contrôle pour déceler les puits non protégés ont été lancées à travers plusieurs wilayas. items.title: Army rescues three injured passengers
items.description: —Launches operation to free two kidnapped victims By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 6, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), have rescued three passengers who sustained gunshot injuries during an attack by suspected kidnappers along the Jos–Makarfi highway in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 1 a.m. on Thursday, September 10, 2026, when troops responded to reports of sporadic shootings by suspected kidnappers who had blocked the highway. On arrival at the scene, the troops found a commercial bus, marked EPE-840XB and driven by Baba Ruwa from Oyo State, which had reportedly been intercepted by the attackers. The suspected kidnappers fled on sighting the troops, enabling the soldiers to rescue three passengers who had sustained gunshot injuries. Further questioning of the rescued passengers revealed that two others, identified as Mrs Precious and Mrs Esther, had allegedly been abducted by the attackers. The three injured passengers were evacuated to the Primary Health Centre, Riyom, for medical attention. The troops have since launched an operation to locate and rescue the two abducted passengers and apprehend the perpetrators. Security sources have also raised concerns over the alleged involvement of militia elements in kidnapping-for-ransom activities in parts of Plateau State. The development, according to the sources, has been compounded by the proliferation of locally fabricated firearms, which they said had increased the capacity of criminal elements to carry out road ambushes and abduct travellers. The sources added that the attackers often exploit their familiarity with the terrain and local communities to evade security forces. Security agencies are intensifying efforts to identify and dismantle the criminal networks, recover illegal weapons and prevent further attacks on motorists and residents.
