Trump’s Dream World in Dallas
items.description: Photographs by Joseph Rushmore P resident Trump began his midterm-convention address last night by casting his spell on the crowd in Dallas. “This place is packed,” he announced from the stage, pointing to the back of the American Airlines Center, where everyone could see hundreds of empty seats. Those who looked up saw thousands more, whole sections without any people at all. But the crowd cheered anyway. A deal had been struck. Reality would be ignored. After more than a decade in politics, Trump is facing his last great electoral test—his popularity is waning, his party is down in the polls, Republicans could lose control in the U.S. House and maybe the Senate. He demanded greater complicity minutes later, seeming to invent a person in the back of the room. “He’s leaving for the bathroom. He’ll be back in two minutes,” he said, pointing. “They’ll take a picture of his seat while he’s gone. And they’ll say Trump did not fill up the arena.” Laughter joined with the cheers for their political wizard. It was working. Trump could say that he had passed “the largest tax cut in the history of our country,” even if that was not the case. He could claim to have won the presidency three times, when he’s actually done so twice. He could describe the recent past as “the most successful two years financially and every other way in the history of the presidency,” despite six in 10 voters saying he had made the economy worse. He could promise to pay every adult U.S. citizen $5,000 if Republicans held both legislative houses, as if that sum did not amount to about 80 percent of the federal discretionary budget. He might even be able to convince the country to embrace the big fantasy, a chance to defy history and seal victory for Republicans in November. “I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot,” he said. “I’m on the ballot. I’m on the ballot. Just one more time.” Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic T he night was all about Trump . He was the alpha and omega, the focus and the solution. Attendees wore pictures of the president on lanyards around their necks, the ticket for entry to the arena. VIP boxes were stocked with Trump was right about everything hats. Oversize photos of the president lined the hallways. Five hours before he arrived, he received his first standing ovation. A video montage played on the big screen, images of the president narrated by a reading of Rudyard Kipling’s “If”—“If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue.” When each speaker dropped Trump’s name, it was cause for riotous celebration. Until now, national political conventions have been held only during presidential-election years, when delegates from each state gather to select their nominee. In the 1970s, the gatherings shifted from smoke-filled rooms for party business to televised infomercials for the candidates. Trump this year created a simulation of a simulation. The balloon nets had no nominee to drop for. The state delegations, sitting under signs on the floor, had no procedural purpose. (The smart party leaders, one strategist told us, were selling their “delegate” tickets to donors.) The convention-in-name-only was for, by, and about one man—who, importantly, cannot be a candidate for president again, according to the U.S. Constitution. [ Read: Trump plans to buy midterm ads about his own record ] “The only way to keep dangerous, radical, weird out of the Senate is a united Republican Party standing with our president, Donald J. Trump,” Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, bellowed from the stage. “Stand for the president, Donald J. Trump. This is a battle for the heart of our nation. I said the heart of our nation.” Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina addresses the audience. No president has tried something like this before. None has had so much money to spend on themselves at this point in a presidency. None has chosen to make the midterms a referendum on themselves while polling so badly. But this is Trump, and Trump has come back from worse. For a decade, the GOP’s electoral success has risen and fallen on his energies. The strategist in chief has bet that turning out Trump voters, the ones who typically stay home when he is not on the ballot, is the only path forward. This is why the first ads he bought for the cycle were not about any candidates who are running this year, but about himself. This was why his latest show was a celebration of the unlimited possibility of his incantations. “Vote Republican, and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come,” he told the crowd. “There’ll be nothing like it.” Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic O utside Trump’s curated fantasy world , not everything has gone according to plan. Trump’s political strategist, James Blair, announced after the off-year elections in 2025 that the president would be “very, very focused on prices and cost of living.” White House aides told us in the new year that the pivot would come after Trump scratched his itch for another confrontation with Iran. By May, as that conflict dragged on, Trump advisers told us quietly that if it had not receded, along with gas prices, by Labor Day, there would be trouble. Two weeks ago, multiple Trump advisers told us they expected the kinetic part of the Iran war to mostly cease in September, clearing the way for lower gas prices. None of that has happened. Missiles are still flying in the Strait of Hormuz. Since the 2025 elections, gas prices have risen 39 percent, from $3.08 to $4.28; 30-year mortgage rates have increased 8 percent; electricity prices have gone up more than 4 percent. Charlie Cook, a political analyst and the dean emeritus of legislative-election handicapping, says that Republicans should brace themselves for a tough result. “The worst-case scenario for the GOP and best for Democrats today would have sounded ludicrous eight months ago,” he wrote recently. “The most plausible today resembles Republicans’ nightmare scenario at the beginning of the year.” [ Read: The YOLO presidency ] Those Republican nightmares, both new and old, are unlikely to be worse than the 40-seat gain made by Democrats in the House of Representatives during Trump’s first term, in 2018, thanks to increased polarization and mid-decennial redistricting. But few Republicans still pretend off-camera that they will be able to maintain control of the House. Narrow Democratic control of the Senate, once outlandish, could be within reach. On the sidelines of the convention in Dallas, strategists muttered about recent polling in House races that shows jump balls where Trump won by double digits in 2024. The outstanding question is whether Democratic candidates can emerge from the dim shadow of President Biden. “While there is a lot of focus on the Republicans’ problems, Democrats have a real problem—they have a real party-image problem,” the Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio told us. Jesse Ferguson, a Democratic strategist, depicts his party in PowerPoint presentations as a backpacker hiking up a steep mountain with gusts of wind at his back. The incline represents Trump’s financial advantages, and the challenge of winning seats in gerrymandered districts and Republican states such as Ohio, Iowa, Texas, and Alaska. The wind is voter sentiment and the enthusiasm advantage inside the Democratic Party. “Democrats have won the message fight. Republicans have lost the governance fight,” he told us. “The question is whether they can use structural advantages to overcome it.” On the whole, Democrats are delighted by Trump’s strategy —to put front and center a man whose unpopularity fires up their voters and further alienates the newly skeptical. “If the Democrats have a great year, it will be because they got their base out to vote in large numbers,” Rich Thau, the moderator of the Swing Voter Project, told us. “It won’t be because they magically converted these swing voters into Democratic senatorial and gubernatorial voters.” Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic But they may not be accounting for Trump’s magic. Two years ago, he bounced back from two impeachments and an attack by his supporters on the U.S. Capitol to win the presidency. Now the odds are against him again. By multiple measures, the president who appeared on the Dallas stage last night had lost a step. When he first won the White House, in 2016, he denounced the folly of distant wars of choice, promised to remedy the reigning economic turmoil of globalization, and boasted of his independence as someone who eschewed campaign donations. A decade later, he is managing a reescalating war in Iran that he started. He has positioned himself as a champion of data centers, the latest lightning rod for populist resentment. And he controls a massive $850 million slush fund he acquired in office through seemingly transactional demands of companies, lobbyists, and wealthy individuals seeking government favor. [ Read: Trump is preparing for a long war ] His economic approval rating this summer, according to Quinnipiac University, stood at 34 percent, down from 53 percent on the eve of the last midterm elections on his watch, in 2018. The 2024 presidential election hinged on the rising cost of living, and after Republicans won the trifecta—the White House and both chambers of Congress—the expectation was that Trump and his party would fix what many still view as Biden’s economy. “I want to emphasize that this wasn’t to just slightly improve things,” David Winston, a Republican strategist who works with congressional leadership, told us. “They viewed a substantive outcome as what they were looking for.” It has not come to pass. T rump has not lost his talent for showmanship. No longer tied to a single hit program in a single slot on NBC, he has spent much of the year creating television spectacles from the Oval Office—a Formula One race, a UFC fight, a Fourth of July party, a World Cup championship celebration where he lingered in the frame. This string of network debuts gave him the confidence to schedule his convention against the first two games of the NFL season. Only Trump would choose to go up against the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots. Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic For those who watched, the first night in Dallas had production quality that has escaped many recent Republican conventions. All the tropes and tricks were hit—the testimonials of a Pennsylvania steelworker and a Florida grandma about policy wins, the glitter reels of alleged Democratic bad behavior, the plea for campaign donations for Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate nominee from Texas. Multiple speakers gave mock “land acknowledgements” praising the national heritage of European colonizers. The comedian Adam Carolla did a bit about Trump’s hair: “You ever see underwater footage of a kelp bed?” There were “everyday Americans,” “American workers,” and Border Patrol agents who gathered onstage, many in work gear. “President Trump refuses to surrender,” Senator Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania said, after a friendly video introduction from his Democratic colleague John Fetterman. “This November there can be no surrender.” Joseph Rushmore for The Atlantic There was even a moment to lay out the core contrast that Trump’s advisers hope will frame the election, the sort of message that any other Republican president in his position would be entirely focused on delivering at this point. In a short video, his team spliced together clips from fringe voices on the left—the “woke,” the America-bashing, the revolutionary—before defining the decision on the ballot. “This is no longer simply Republican versus Democrat, or conservative versus liberal,” said the voice-over. “Today the choice is unmistakable: extreme versus mainstream.” But the centerpiece remained Trump. Speaker after speaker described him in near-messianic terms. “As it turns out, Washington wasn’t incapable of working for the American people; all we needed was a new president,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said. T. W. Shannon, a candidate for lieutenant governor in Oklahoma, placed the entire GOP in the president’s shadow. “We’re also the party of the greatest president in American history, President Donald J. Trump,” he declared. But no comments mattered more than Trump’s. He talked for nearly two hours, a rolicking, weaving address that only occasionally stuck to the teleprompter. It ended where he began. “Please pretend that I’m running, and get out and vote on November 3 or sooner,” he said. “Because, in actuality, I really am running.” In actuality, he is not. Or maybe he is, in a way. His crowd remained in their seats to the end. The room, at times, felt packed to the rafters. Additional reporting by Jack Rodriquez-Vars

items.title: Ghana pushes China for deeper mining partnerships, value addition
items.description: Ghana is seeking deeper mining partnerships with China, with the government urging Chinese investors to move beyond the extraction and export of raw minerals and invest in processing, technology transfer, skills development and local supply chains. The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, made the call when he addressed the Ministerial Forum on International Mining Cooperation and the opening of the 28th China Mining Conference and Exhibition (CHINA MINING 2026) in Tianjin, China. Representing President John Dramani Mahama and the Ghanaian government, Mr Buah said Ghana was seeking a new generation of mining partnerships that would ensure greater value was retained in the country while providing investors with a stable and commercially viable operating environment. He said Ghana’s mineral resources must be used to drive industrialisation, create jobs and build local expertise rather than continue to be exported largely as raw materials. “The next chapter of mining must be measured not simply by what we take from the ground, but by what we leave above it: industries, skills, technology, restored land, stronger communities and a more prosperous nation,” he said. Ghana seeks value addition Mr Buah said Ghana was determined to move away from a model in which resource-rich countries exported raw materials while most processing and value creation occurred elsewhere. He said the government wanted future mining partnerships to support domestic processing, industrial development, job creation and skills development. “For the young Ghanaian looking for work, value addition is not an economic theory. It is a job. It is a skill. It is a career. It is the possibility of building a life at home,” he said. The Minister said Ghana was reviewing its mining regulatory framework, formalising artisanal and small-scale mining and strengthening transparency and responsible oversight across the gold value chain. He also cited the presence of major Chinese mining companies, including Chifeng Gold Group, Shandong Gold and Zijin Mining, in Ghana as evidence of the potential for deeper cooperation. “We want the next generation of partnerships to go further into processing, technology, skills development, infrastructure and local supply chains,” Mr Buah said. He said China’s experience in linking natural resources to processing, manufacturing, infrastructure and technology offered opportunities for Ghana. “The question is no longer only, ‘Who will buy our resources?’ The more consequential question is: ‘What can we build together from them?’” he asked. Green and intelligent mining Mr Buah also called for greater Ghana-China cooperation in environmental management and the adoption of modern technologies in mining. He cited the establishment of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and the advancement of the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme (rCOMSDEP) as part of the government’s efforts to strengthen responsible and formalised small-scale mining. He said environmental protection must remain central to Ghana’s mining agenda, particularly in addressing the effects of illegal and irresponsible mining. “A river is not simply an environmental statistic. It is drinking water. It is farming. It is the livelihood of a community. It is an inheritance held in trust for a child not yet born,” he said. The Minister called for cooperation in areas including mine reclamation, tailings management and land restoration, drawing on China’s technological experience. He also said Ghana was modernising its national geological database, improving geological survey and mapping capabilities and strengthening digital traceability across the gold supply chain. According to him, better geological data would reduce exploration risks, improve government decision-making and help investors make informed decisions. He identified China’s expertise in automation, geological science, mineral processing, data systems, engineering and infrastructure as areas that could support Ghana’s transition towards more intelligent mining. Mr Buah stressed, however, that technology partnerships must also build local capacity. “We want structured technical exchanges and mining-specific training opportunities for Ghanaian engineers, geologists and regulators, so that cooperation leaves behind stronger Ghanaian expertise and institutions,” he said. Ghana showcases investment opportunities Ghana’s participation in CHINA MINING 2026 is also being used to showcase investment opportunities in the country’s mineral sector through Ghana Mining Day. The programme, themed “Building Ghana’s Next Frontier: Geology, Value Addition and Investment Partnership,” is expected to highlight opportunities for international investors. Mr Buah identified gold refining, an integrated aluminium industry, iron ore development and critical minerals as key areas for Ghana’s next phase of mineral development. He said Ghana wanted to develop its iron ore resources to support domestic steel production and position its critical minerals sector to contribute to emerging industries and technologies. Deepening Ghana-China mining ties Mr Buah described Ghana and China as longstanding partners, noting that bilateral relations had expanded over more than six decades from diplomacy into trade, education, infrastructure and other areas of cooperation. He urged Chinese investors and international mining companies to view Ghana as a strategic destination for long-term investment. “We have the resources. China has deep experience in capital, technology, processing, infrastructure and industrial development. Between us lies an opportunity to build commercially sound partnerships in which Ghana creates more value at home, investors succeed, communities share in prosperity, and both countries emerge stronger,” he said. The Minister said Ghana’s objective was to ensure that mining generated lasting benefits beyond the lifespan of individual mines. “Our responsibility is to ensure that long after the mines have closed, the prosperity they created is still alive,” he said.

Neuf pyromanes présumés ont été arrêtés et placés sous mandat de dépôt, a indiqué ce jeudi le parquet antiterroriste du tribunal de Sidi M’hamed d’Alger. Ils sont soupçonnés d’avoir participé aux incendies qui ont endeuillé la wilaya de Jijel fin août. Plus de détails à venir. L’article ALERTE. Incendies de Jijel : neuf pyromanes présumés écroués est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: UTAG-KNUST escalates Pro-VC, Dean appointment dispute to University Council
items.description: The University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG) at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has escalated its dispute over the appointment of Pro-Vice Chancellors and Deans to the University Council. The move follows what the Association describes as a “deeply disappointing” decision by the Academic Board at its September 9, 2026 meeting. In a letter to UTAG-KNUST members dated September 10, the Association’s President, Prof. Eric Kwabena Kyeh Abavare, and Secretary, Prof. Akwasi Afrifa Acheampong, said the Academic Board had failed to uphold UTAG’s position that the existing appointment process should remain unchanged until a mutually acceptable framework was agreed. UTAG-KNUST said it would now formally engage the University Council to seek an urgent reconsideration of the matter. “Leadership considers this outcome deeply disappointing, and believes it warrants a firm but measured response from the Association,” the letter stated. The Association argued that its demand for meaningful participation in decisions concerning the leadership of academic staff is grounded in Act 1157, Clause 5(f). It said the dispute was therefore not merely about procedure but concerned the broader principle of collegial governance at the university. “This is more than a procedural disagreement,” UTAG-KNUST said. The Association warned that allowing the position of academic staff to be set aside in the appointment of Pro-Vice Chancellors and Deans could create a precedent that affects other areas of university governance. It also rejected the suggestion that the university’s strategic plan could override its statutory framework. “A strategic plan, however important it is, and with an expected life span of about ten years, cannot properly override a statute whose life span is measured in decades,” the Association said. UTAG-KNUST said it would ask the University Council to consider four key issues. They include the statutory basis of its membership under Act 1157, Clause 5(f), and the democratic rights it says flow from that provision. The Association is also seeking recognition of members’ right to have a genuine vote in the appointment of Pro-Vice Chancellors and Deans. It wants clarity on the relationship between the university’s statutes and its strategic plan, arguing that the latter should not displace the former. The preservation of collegial governance as a defining feature of KNUST is also among its concerns. Despite the escalation, UTAG-KNUST said it remained committed to dialogue and would approach its engagement with the Council in good faith. “We will continue to prefer dialogue, and approach these engagements in good faith and with the respect due to sister stakeholders,” the letter stated. The Association said any appointment process adopted by Management should provide a genuine role for key stakeholders who would work with and be led by the officers appointed. It described such participation as consistent with the university’s established practice. UTAG-KNUST has meanwhile urged its members to maintain a united position, discuss the matter within their departments and faculties, and remain patient while being prepared to act if necessary. Members were also asked to refer individual approaches from Management on the matter to the Association’s executives to ensure consistency in UTAG-KNUST’s position. The letter was copied to the Chairman of the University Council, the Vice-Chancellor, the Registrar and the National UTAG Executive. The University Council is expected to consider UTAG-KNUST’s request for reconsideration as the dispute over the appointment process continues.

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : clôture dans le rouge
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé dans le rouge jeudi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,27% à 18.785,4 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a diminué de 0,27% à 1.353,07 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,08% à 1.401,47 pts. De son côté, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a baissé de 0,32% à 1.808,1 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Sylviculture et papier » (-4,12%), « Matériels, logiciels et services informatiques » (-2,07%) et « Pétrole et gaz » (-0,76%) ont accusé les plus forts replis. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Chimie » (+1,79%), « Loisirs et hôtels » (+1,56%) et « Industrie pharmaceutique » (+1,38%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 248,41 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central et dominés par les transactions sur Managem (116,64 MDH), CFG Bank (18,59 MDH) et TGCC S.A (16,98 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est, quant à elle, établie à plus de 1.105,91 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par Med Paper (-4,12% à 24,65 DH), SMI (-3,65% à 6.600 DH), HPS (-2,99% à 650 DH), TotalEnergies Marketing Maroc (-2,21% à 1.503 DH) et Involys (-2,09% à 126,3 DH). En revanche, BMCI (+2,45% à 618,9 DH), SNEP (+2,05% à 349 DH), Cartier Saada (+2,05% à 22,45 DH), Risma (+1,56% à 326 DH) et Sothema (+1,47% à 364,9 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. The post Bourse de Casablanca : clôture dans le rouge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Boulgou/Tenkodogo : le cheikh Idrissa Moné offre six tonnes de ciment à l’agence Faso Mêbo
items.description: BURKINA-DON-CIMENT-EMBELLISSEMENT-COMMUNE-TENKODOGO Boulgou/Tenkodogo : le cheikh Idrissa Moné offre six tonnes de ciment à l'agence Faso Mêbo Tenkodogo, 09 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le commandant adjoint de l’agence Faso Mêbo de Tenkodogo, l’adjudant-chef Inoussa Kanazoé, a réceptionné mercredi à Sabtenga, dans la commune de Tenkodogo, un don de six tonnes de ciment et de trois voyages de gravier offerts par le cheikh Idrissa Moné. Le don est destiné à soutenir les travaux d’embellissement de la cité de Naaba Zoungrana, dans le cadre de l’initiative Faso Mêbo. Selon le donateur, son geste est motivé par la volonté d’accompagner une action d’intérêt communautaire, conformément aux valeurs et aux enseignements reçus de ses parents. « Quand vous voyez quelqu’un faire un travail utile pour toute la collectivité, il faut lui apporter votre aide, selon le peu que vous avez », a déclaré le cheikh Idrissa Moné. A l’en croire, il a invité ses fidèles à adhérer à l’initiative, dès qu’il en a eu connaissance. « Si les personnes âgées ne peuvent plus participer physiquement aux travaux, elles peuvent néanmoins contribuer par des encouragements, aux plans moral et matériel, pour galvaniser ceux qui sont sur le terrain », a-t-il indiqué. A travers ce geste, le cheikh Moné entend également inviter les autres à s’inscrire dans la même dynamique. « J’appelle les communautés religieuses à suivre notre exemple en accompagnant la construction du pays », a-t-il exhorté. Présent à Sabtenga pour la circonstance, l’adjudant-chef Kanazoé a réceptionné le don au nom de l’agence Faso Mêbo. Le donateur a fait savoir que cette contribution constitue une première étape. Il a exprimé sa volonté de poursuivre son engagement en faveur de l’initiative, ce selon ses moyens. Agence d’Information du Burkina SM/ata/zs

items.title: Allianz Trade : cinq secteurs marocains confrontés à des fragilités persistantes
items.description: Aucun des secteurs analysés au Maroc n’est placé en situation de risque élevé dans le nouvel Atlas sectoriel d’Allianz Trade. La photographie n’en est pas pour autant uniformément favorable. Cinq branches : l’énergie, le transport, le textile, les métaux et la construction, concentrent les vulnérabilités les plus marquées dans un environnement mondial bouleversé par les tensions commerciales, la recomposition industrielle et les nouvelles exigences de financement. Le Maroc présente un profil sectoriel globalement contenu, mais traversé par des lignes de fragilité bien identifiées. C’est ce qui ressort du Sector Atlas 2026 publié par Allianz Trade, qui examine les risques auxquels sont exposées les entreprises dans 18 grands secteurs et les classe selon quatre niveaux, du risque faible au risque élevé. Le Royaume ne compte aucun secteur dans la dernière catégorie, celle d’une crise imminente ou déjà avérée. Cinq activités se distinguent toutefois par un classement en « risque sensible », un niveau qui renvoie à des faiblesses structurelles et à des perspectives moins favorables pour les entreprises. Il s’agit de la construction, du transport, du textile, des métaux et de l’énergie. Cette cartographie intervient dans une économie mondiale que l’assureur-crédit décrit comme évoluant désormais à plusieurs rythmes. La croissance mondiale devrait ralentir à 2,5% en 2026 avant de remonter à 2,9% en 2027, avec une dynamique largement soutenue par les investissements liés à l’intelligence artificielle. Cette accélération technologique ne bénéficie cependant pas de manière uniforme aux secteurs et aux économies. Construction et énergie, deux secteurs sous contraintes La construction figure parmi les principales activités marocaines classées en risque sensible. À l’échelle mondiale, Allianz Trade souligne la persistance de plusieurs facteurs de vulnérabilité : coût du financement, exigences élevées en fonds de roulement, pression sur les marges et risques liés à l’exécution des projets. Le secteur bénéficie certes d’importants relais de croissance dans les infrastructures, l’énergie et les équipements numériques. Mais la demande privée, notamment dans l’immobilier résidentiel et commercial, demeure particulièrement sensible aux conditions de financement. Cette situation revêt une attention particulière au Maroc, où la construction se trouve à la croisée d’investissements publics importants et d’un marché privé plus dépendant de la dynamique du crédit et de la demande immobilière. Dans son analyse consacrée au pays, Allianz Trade relève d’ailleurs que les difficultés rencontrées dans la construction figurent parmi les facteurs pesant sur la situation des entreprises. L’énergie apparaît également dans la catégorie du risque sensible. Le contraste observé à l’échelle mondiale est particulièrement marqué. Les acteurs du pétrole et du gaz conservent une capacité de génération de trésorerie solide dans un contexte de prix élevés, tandis que le secteur des renouvelables reste confronté à des besoins d’investissement considérables, à des coûts de financement élevés et aux contraintes des réseaux électriques. Paradoxalement, la même transformation technologique qui alimente le supercycle de l’intelligence artificielle ouvre de nouveaux besoins énergétiques. La multiplication des centres de données renforce ainsi la demande d’électricité et accroît les besoins d’investissement dans la production, les réseaux et le stockage. Textile et transport face à un environnement plus instable Le classement du textile parmi les secteurs sensibles intervient alors que l’industrie mondiale de l’habillement est confrontée à une double pression : celle des coûts et celle de l’évolution des comportements de consommation. La hausse ou la volatilité des prix de l’énergie et des matières premières reste difficile à absorber dans une industrie caractérisée par une forte concurrence et une capacité limitée à relever les prix. Dans le même temps, la demande évolue sous l’effet de la recherche de produits moins chers, de l’essor de la seconde main et d’une plus grande prudence des ménages dans plusieurs marchés. Pour une industrie marocaine fortement connectée à la demande européenne, ces évolutions mondiales constituent un élément de vigilance. Le textile et l’habillement demeurent d’ailleurs parmi les principales catégories d’exportation du Maroc, ce qui expose directement une partie de la filière aux transformations du marché européen. Le transport, autre secteur classé en risque sensible, évolue quant à lui dans un environnement où les tensions géopolitiques peuvent rapidement modifier les coûts et les itinéraires. Les perturbations des routes maritimes, les prix de l’énergie et l’incertitude commerciale continuent de peser sur les équilibres économiques des opérateurs. Allianz Trade décrit plus largement un secteur mondial en pleine transformation, confronté simultanément aux exigences de résilience des chaînes logistiques, aux tensions géopolitiques et à la nécessité d’investir dans de nouveaux modèles opérationnels. Les métaux entre opportunités stratégiques et vulnérabilités Le classement des métaux en risque sensible illustre, lui aussi, une évolution moins linéaire qu’il n’y paraît. Certains segments bénéficient d’une dynamique structurelle favorable, notamment ceux liés à l’électrification, aux infrastructures énergétiques et au développement technologique. Allianz Trade met notamment en avant la demande associée au cuivre, au lithium et aux terres rares, stimulée par la transition énergétique et les besoins croissants en infrastructures numériques. D’autres segments, à l’inverse, restent confrontés à une demande industrielle plus fragile et à des conditions de marché difficiles. Cette différence entre les différentes branches métallurgiques résume en partie le nouveau paysage décrit par l’Atlas : la transition technologique ne crée pas un cycle de croissance généralisé, mais redistribue les opportunités entre activités, entreprises et chaînes de valeur. Un paysage sectoriel contrasté Derrière ces cinq secteurs sensibles, la carte marocaine dessinée par Allianz Trade reste néanmoins plus nuancée. Quatre activités bénéficient d’un classement en risque faible : l’agroalimentaire, le pharmaceutique, les logiciels et services informatiques ainsi que l’informatique et les télécommunications. Entre ces deux groupes, plusieurs pans de l’économie productive sont placés en risque moyen, notamment l’automobile, la chimie, l’électronique, le papier, la distribution, les machines et équipements, l’équipement de transport et l’équipement ménager. La lecture de l’Atlas ne dessine donc pas une économie marocaine en difficulté généralisée. Elle met plutôt en évidence une fragmentation croissante des trajectoires sectorielles. Certains secteurs continuent de bénéficier d’une demande structurellement solide ou de nouveaux cycles d’investissement liés au numérique. D’autres restent plus directement exposés au coût du capital, à la volatilité énergétique, à la pression concurrentielle ou aux transformations du commerce mondial. The post Allianz Trade : cinq secteurs marocains confrontés à des fragilités persistantes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Une clinique clandestine démantelée au quartier Diaradougou
items.description: Une intervention des autorités administratives de la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso a permis de fermer une clinique clandestine opérant dans le quartier Diaradougou. L’opération a permis de mettre en lumière un établissement fonctionnant dans des conditions sanitaires déplorables et dispensant des soins hors de tout cadre légal et sécuritaire. Le Directeur régional de la Santé du Guiriko, le Président de la Délégation Spéciale (PDS) de l’Arrondissement n°1, ainsi que la Brigade Laabal étaient présents sur les lieux afin de constater les faits et procéder aux vérifications nécessaires. Les autorités ont relevé de graves manquements à l’hygiène ainsi que des risques majeurs pour la sécurité des patients pris en charge. A l’issue de cette descente, le responsable de l’établissement clandestin a été interpelé et conduit à la Brigade Labaaal. Ce demantellent met en évidence les dangers de la médecine illégal. La santé des citoyens exige un suivi strict, des infrastructures conformes et un personnel qualifié. Cet évèment rappelle la nécessité de renforcer les contrôles des structures de soin et de maintenir une vigilance constante pour éradiquer ces pratiques illégales et protéger la population Source : Liberté Communication.

items.title: CRIEF : Kassory et Damaro autorisés à quitter la Guinée pour des soins
items.description: L'ancien Premier ministre Dr Ibrahima Kassory Fofana et l'ancien président de l'Assemblée nationale, Amadou Damaro Camara sont autorisés à quitter la Guinée pour recevoir des soins médicaux à l’étranger. L’information a été confirmée ce jeudi 10 septembre 2026 à Guinéenews par le procureur spécial près la CRIEF, Alphonse Charles Wright, joint par téléphone. Le parquet spécial a requis la mise en œuvre de cette autorisation auprès du commissaire spécial de l’aéroport international Ahmed-Sékou-Touré et du directeur central de la police aux frontières. Condamnés en appel dans des procédures devant la CRIEF, les deux anciens hauts responsables avaient invoqué leur état de santé et la nécessité d’une prise en charge médicale spécialisée à l’étranger. Cette autorisation de sortie du territoire ne met toutefois pas fin aux procédures judiciaires engagées à leur encontre. Les deux hommes restent soumis aux décisions et obligations de la justice guinéenne.

items.title: DKM boss Delle K. Martin withdraws from Nandom NPP primaries
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of DKM Microfinance Company and New Patriotic Party (NPP) stalwart in Nandom, Delle K. Martin, has withdrawn from the party’s parliamentary primaries in the Nandom Constituency. In a statement issued on Thursday, September 10, Mr Martin said his decision followed careful reflection and extensive consultations with his family, elders, friends, associates and party members. “After careful reflection and extensive consultations… I have decided to withdraw my intention to contest the New Patriotic Party parliamentary primaries for the Nandom constituency,” he stated. He said his decision to step aside was intended to promote unity and advance the long-term interests of the NPP and the Nandom Constituency. Nandom primaries now a three-horse race Mr Martin’s withdrawal leaves three aspirants in the race for the NPP parliamentary ticket in Nandom: Ambrose Dery – former Interior Minister and former Member of Parliament for Nandom Alex K. Mohl – Development Consultant Sylvester Isaing – Legal Practitioner Mr Martin has pledged his support for whoever emerges as the party’s candidate, saying he would work with the eventual winner to support NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the 2028 general election. “I will support any of the contestants that will emerge as a candidate of the NPP to partner Dr Bawumia to win the 2028 general election. May the best aspirant win,” he said. He also appealed to his supporters to respect his decision and support the eventual winner of the primaries. “I remain committed to contributing to the growth and welfare of Nandom and to working within the party for a brighter future for our people,” he added. Reaffirming his commitment to the NPP, Mr Martin said his withdrawal was not a departure from the party, indicating that he could seek the parliamentary ticket in the future. “I will come back to contest next time for I remain a card-bearing member of the Great NPP,” he said.

items.title: Boulgou : le Conseil supérieur de la communication renforce les capacités de 35 acteurs des médias et du numérique à Tenkodogo
items.description: ‎BURKINA-FORMATION-MEDIAS-NUMERIQUE-TENKODOGO Boulgou : le Conseil supérieur de la communication renforce les capacités de 35 acteurs des médias et du numérique à Tenkodogo ‎Tenkodogo, 9 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC) a organisé, du 7 au 9 septembre 2026 à Tenkodogo, un atelier de formation et de sensibilisation de 35 journalistes et web activistes sur leur responsabilité sociale en période de crise. ‎Après Bobo-Dioulasso et Koudougou, Tenkodogo a accueilli la troisième phase de cette activité qui a réuni des professionnels des médias et du numérique des régions du Nakambé, du Goulmou, du Kuilsé, de l’Oubri, de la Sirba, de la Tapoa et du Yaadga. ‎La cérémonie d’ouverture, présidée par le Président du CSC, Wendingoundi Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, a été marquée par l’exécution de l’hymne national et les interventions du gouverneur du Nakambé, Yiyé Abraham Somdo, et du représentant du Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD), Dieudonné Kini. ‎Le camarade gouverneur a souhaité une bonne session aux participants, avant de les inviter à profiter de leur séjour à Tenkodogo et de les rassurer quant à leur sécurité. Abraham Somdo a d’ailleurs salué le travail mené par les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). ‎Pour le représentant du PNUD, « le développement humain durable n'est possible que dans une société de paix, de tolérance et de cohésion sociale », où les citoyens ont accès à une information fiable et de qualité. Selon ses explications, ce point rejoint l’objectif de développement durable 16, relatif à la paix, à la justice et à des institutions efficaces. ‎S’appuyant sur le verset biblique « la mort et la vie sont au pouvoir de la langue » (Proverbes 18:21), Dieudonné Kini a invité les journalistes et web activistes à mesurer leur responsabilité dans la diffusion de l’information. ‎ « Par votre professionnalisme, votre respect des règles déontologiques et votre engagement en faveur de la vérité et de la défense de l’intérêt général, vous contribuez à renforcer la confiance entre les citoyens et les institutions », a-t-il conclu. ‎La communication inaugurale, intitulée « La responsabilité sociale du journaliste ou du web-activiste dans la gestion de l’information en période de crise », a été présentée par l’expert en STIC, Moussa Sawadogo. ‎Les trois jours de travaux ont porté sur neuf modules. Il s’agit notamment du rôle du CSC dans la régulation de l’information en période de crise, de la couverture médiatique des attaques terroristes, la gestion des émissions d’expression directe, la promotion de la cohésion sociale, la manipulation de l’information à l’ère de l’intelligence artificielle, du fact-checking et de l’investigation numérique (OSINT). ‎La sécurité numérique et la cybercriminalité, la répression de la désinformation et des discours de haine, ainsi que le pacte des médias burkinabè pour une communication de guerre contre le terrorisme et la reconquête du territoire national ont également été abordés. ‎Ces modules ont été animés par plusieurs experts, dont Abdoulaye Dao, directeur général de la publicité et de l’observation des contenus du CSC, le lieutenant-colonel Abdoul Azize Ouédraogo, directeur de la communication et des relations publiques des armées burkinabè, Sa Majesté le Dawelg Naaba Boalga, Alain Dabilgou, expert en veille médiatique, Isidore Bouda, président de l'association Fasocheck, le capitaine de police Emmanuel Nacoulma de la BCLCC, et K. Raymond Sanogo, président du TGI de Tenkodogo. ‎À la clôture, le directeur de cabinet du président du CSC, Fousseni Kindo, a lu le discours du président de l’institution. Celui-ci a réaffirmé l’engagement de son organisation à poursuivre le renforcement des capacités des professionnels des médias et des acteurs de la communication. ‎« Nous continuerons, avec l’appui de nos partenaires, à créer des cadres de dialogue, de formation et d’échanges afin d’accompagner l’évolution des pratiques médiatiques et de relever les défis liés à la gestion de notre espace civique numérique », a-t-il déclaré. ‎Dans leur motion de remerciement, les participants ont salué l’initiative du Conseil et de ses partenaires ainsi que l’accompagnement des autorités du Nakambé. Ils ont promis de faire du professionnalisme leur leitmotiv. Agence d’Information du Burkina (AIB) JPB/ata/zs

items.title: PMDC directs universities to ensure smooth and transparent conduct of MDCAT
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) on Thursday directed universities to ensure that the Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT), scheduled for September 20, is conducted in a smooth and transparent manner. Passing the MDCAT is mandatory for admission to medical and dental colleges in Pakistan. Every year, up to 200,000 candidates appear for the test, while around 25,000 secure seats in public-sector and private medical and dental colleges. The instructions were given by PMDC President Prof Dr Rizwan Taj during a meeting attended by the vice chancellors of universities conducting the examination, where preparations were reviewed to ensure that all necessary arrangements were in place nationwide, according to a statement . A total of 138,158 candidates have registered for the 2026 MDCAT, which will be conducted in 35 cities and towns across Pakistan, as well as at an international centre in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Taj informed the meeting that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had also directed that the MDCAT be conducted smoothly, in a highly transparent, fair and orderly manner, with zero tolerance for any compromise on its integrity. The statement added that he had emphasised strict adherence to policies and guidelines. Moreover, the meeting reviewed arrangements for medical support, emergency response and facilitation services at examination centres to ensure a safe and conducive environment for all candidates, including those from Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The participating universities and provincial authorities were advised to ensure that examination centres were adequately prepared, with appropriate seating, essential facilities, security measures and necessary arrangements for candidates and their accompanying parents or guardians. The PMDC said it had provided unified regulatory standards for the MDCAT papers, while responsibility for the on-ground conduct and administrative arrangements of the examination, including ensuring the transparency of the process and the secrecy of the papers at the respective centres, rested with the provincial authorities and universities. The vice chancellors and representatives of the provincial authorities assured the PMDC president that all these requirements would be met and the necessary arrangements completed in time. Earlier this week, the Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) called for complete transparency and foolproof security in MDCAT, while demanding an immediate independent forensic audit of private medical and dental colleges across the country. In a statement, PMA Secretary General Dr Abdul Ghafoor Shoro reiterated the association’s longstanding concerns over the country’s reliance on high-stakes entrance examinations as the primary mechanism for selecting students for medical education. Dr Shoro said repeated controversies surrounding the MDCAT — including allegations of paper leaks, administrative mismanagement and other irregularities involving different testing bodies in previous years — had undermined public confidence in the examination process. Additionally, the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) health secretary had met PMDC officials and highlighted the difficulties being faced by students in completing their MDCAT registration due to the prolonged internet shutdown in the region. PMDC officials had vowed to provide all possible facilitation to the candidates. Last month, a subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Health expressed concern over increasing complaints regarding the conduct of the MDCAT and its scheduled date. Govt urged to allow Afghans to complete studies Meanwhile, the Pakistan Islamic Medical Association (PIMA) expressed serious concern over directives requiring Afghan medical students enrolled in public and private medical universities in Pakistan to leave the country, calling for a review of the decision on humanitarian and educational grounds. In a statement on Thursday, PIMA Acting President Prof Muhammad Tayyab said Afghan students whose medical education and training were currently in progress and whose educational and legal documentation was complete should be allowed to complete their studies. He added that abruptly interrupting their education would leave their academic and professional futures uncertain, while Afghanistan was already facing a severe shortage of doctors and healthcare professionals. “Afghan students who complete their medical education in Pakistan can return to their country in the future and play an important role in meeting the healthcare needs of its people”, the association said. PIMA stressed that political disputes and prevailing circumstances should not be allowed to affect healthcare, treatment, education or the future of students. It added that they should be given the opportunity to complete their professional education and build their futures. The association urged the government to review the decision in light of humanitarian considerations, continuity of education and the healthcare needs of the region, and to allow Afghan medical students currently enrolled in Pakistani institutions to complete their studies.

items.title: L'été se prolonge à Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort
items.description: Alors que la rentrée marque la fin des vacances pour beaucoup, Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort prolonge l’esprit de l’été sur la côte Atlantique et invite à savourer encore quelques parenthèses de douceur face à l’océan. Dans un cadre privilégié, le resort continue de proposer une expérience complète autour du bien-être, de la gastronomie, du sport et des moments à partager en famille. Les restaurants de plage restent ouverts aux clients du resort comme aux visiteurs extérieurs, offrant l’occasion de profiter pleinement du cadre balnéaire et des dernières belles journées de la saison. Le golf, les activités sportives et les expériences en plein air viennent compléter cette échappée entre terre et océan. Le Mazagan Spa poursuit également l’enrichissement de son offre avec de nouvelles expériences et des marques internationales reconnues, pour une expérience dédiée au bien-être et à la beauté. Parmi les dernières nouveautés, 111SKIN, marque britannique de skincare haut de gamme, rejoint l’offre du Spa, aux côtés de MY.ORGANICS, marque italienne de soins capillaires professionnels formulés à partir d’ingrédients d’origine naturelle et d’extraits botaniques. Pour accompagner cette envie de prolonger les beaux jours, Mazagan propose l'offre « Séjour Océan à Mazagan », comprenant jusqu’à 20 % de réduction sur l’hébergement et les soins Spa, ainsi que jusqu’à 10 % sur une sélection d’activités sportives. L’offre inclut également le petit-déjeuner pour 2 adultes et 2 enfants de moins de 12 ans, permettant aux familles de profiter pleinement d’un séjour placé sous le signe de la détente et du partage. A Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort, l’été ne s’arrête pas avec la rentrée. Il se prolonge au rythme de l’océan, des moments de bien-être et des expériences à vivre et à partager, le temps d’une escapade sur la côte Atlantique. items.title: Burkina : Le Salon panafricain des personnes âgées met le numérique au cœur de sa 3e édition
items.description: La 3e édition du Salon panafricain des personnes âgées (SPA) a été officiellement lancée, ce 10 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Organisé par la structure Faso Events, le rendez-vous entend mettre les seniors au cœur des réflexions sur l’inclusion numérique et la solidarité intergénérationnelle. Prévue du 7 au 10 octobre 2026 à la salle des conférences de Ouaga 2000, cette édition se tient sous le thème « Seniors et société numérique : un levier stratégique d’inclusion et de valorisation des seniors plutôt qu’un facteur supplémentaire de marginalisation ». À travers cette thématique, les initiateurs souhaitent ouvrir un espace de dialogue et de réflexion sur la place des personnes âgées dans une société de plus en plus numérique. Le SPA 2026 ambitionne également de favoriser les échanges entre les différentes générations. L’objectif est de promouvoir une meilleure inclusion des seniors et de valoriser leur contribution à la société. Un espace de transmission entre générations Le SPA se veut avant tout, selon Yacine Kindo Zetiyenga, directrice générale de Faso Events, un cadre de valorisation des personnes âgées et de transmission intergénérationnelle. Les seniors y sont appelés à partager avec la jeunesse leurs savoirs et les valeurs culturelles, sociales et traditionnelles. La programmation prévoit plusieurs activités. Il est notamment annoncé un village santé avec des consultations médicales gratuites. Des espaces d’exposition, des ateliers pratiques, ainsi qu’un village gastronomique et un village ludique sont également prévus. Le public pourra aussi découvrir des objets anciens et participer à des excursions touristiques. Le programme comprend en outre le bal des seniors, innovation de cette édition, un défilé de mode et des remises de distinctions. Ces différentes activités visent à offrir aux participants un cadre à la fois instructif, culturel et récréatif. Le numérique au cœur des échanges La promotrice souligne par ailleurs la place accordée au numérique cette année. Elle estime que les personnes âgées doivent pouvoir mieux comprendre les évolutions technologiques et les intégrer dans leur quotidien. Cette orientation répond également à l’intérêt manifesté par certains seniors pour des sujets comme l’intelligence artificielle. « Nos seniors ont besoin d’être au courant, d’être informés de toutes ces innovations technologiques, afin de pouvoir les intégrer dans leur quotidien » , a-t-elle déclaré. Yacine Kindo Zetiyenga a invité les différentes catégories de la population à prendre part au rendez-vous. L’accès au salon étant gratuit, elle appelle le public à se mobiliser. « Toutes les couches sociales, toutes les tranches d’âge sont attendues à cette troisième édition » , a-t-elle ajouté. Pour elle, l’événement doit surtout permettre de renforcer le lien entre les générations, chacune pouvant apprendre de l’autre. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article Burkina : Le Salon panafricain des personnes âgées met le numérique au cœur de sa 3e édition est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: APC to receive 10,000 new members
items.description: —MJB Movement plans mass defection from ADC, PDP, NDC ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC) has said it is ready to receive and integrate more than 10,000 members of various political parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), into its structures. The planned defection is being coordinated by the Maji Johnson Bello (MJB) Movement and is expected to culminate in a formal ceremony following ongoing consultations with the APC leadership. Executive members of the Movement visited the APC National Secretariat in Abuja on Tuesday as part of preparations for the formal defection. Receiving the delegation on behalf of the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, his Personal Private Secretary, Comrade Jibrin Bancir, described the development as a significant boost to the party’s grassroots mobilisation. Bancir said the APC was encouraged by the organisational capacity, grassroots reach and political network being brought into the party by the MJB Movement. He assured the incoming members that the party would provide mechanisms for their seamless integration into its structures, beginning from the ward level. “We are delighted by the huge capacity that the MJB Movement is bringing to the table. The APC is ready to receive and integrate all of you into the structures of the party. “We will work out the necessary procedures to ensure that everybody has a place to operate and contribute meaningfully at the local level,” he said. Bancir stressed the importance of grassroots participation in politics, saying the new members would be properly registered and integrated into the party at the ward, local government, state and national levels. “Politics is local. We will ensure that everybody knows you in your local government as bona fide members of the APC,” he added. He urged the leadership of the MJB Movement to sustain its mobilisation efforts, assuring them of institutional support from the APC leadership during the transition. Earlier, Chairman of the MJB Movement, Maji Johnson Bello, said the decision to join the APC was based on the group’s belief that the economic reforms being implemented by President Bola Tinubu offered a realistic pathway to addressing the country’s economic challenges. Bello said members of the Movement had examined the situation in the country and concluded that the administration’s reform agenda deserved the support of Nigerians seeking a stronger and more productive economy. He said the Movement was not joining the APC merely for political convenience, but had taken a deliberate decision to support what it described as the administration’s efforts to reposition the economy and lay the foundation for sustainable development. According to him, the MJB Movement would deploy its grassroots network to mobilise more Nigerians into the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We have taken time to examine the situation in the country and the reforms being undertaken by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. We are convinced that the direction of the administration offers Nigeria the best opportunity to overcome its present economic realities and build a stronger future,” Bello said. He said the forthcoming defection would mark the beginning of a broader mobilisation campaign, adding that the Movement would continue to engage Nigerians at the grassroots and encourage them to support President Tinubu and the APC. Bello also expressed confidence in the Movement’s capacity to bring thousands of politically active Nigerians into the ruling party and strengthen its structures across the country. FO says Makkah defence pact 'defensive' in nature, expansion currently 'not on the cards'
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday that the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “defensive” in nature, adding that expansion of the pact was currently “not on the cards”. FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks while addressing a weekly press briefing. He said that the pact was primarily a “defensive alliance to ensure regional security primarily through deterrence”. He said that expansion of the pact was currently “not on the cards”, adding that “Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye must first further consolidate their organisation and cooperation”. He said that following the consolidation, the agreement will be “open to all countries that share similar stances and perspectives”. The spokesperson said that the three member states were holding consultations at various levels under the framework. He reiterated that the states will make a decision on the agreement’s expansion at a later stage. “At this stage, there are no discussions regarding the expansion of the Makkah agreement,” he said. He said information on future meetings will be shared “on an ongoing basis”, adding that exact timing was not yet known. Khan said the pact was in the initial stage of formation and detailed consultations on “its structure, procedures and other matters” will be held. “Significant work lies ahead to finalise the organisation’s structure, mechanisms, and procedures,” he said, adding that any future developments will become clear in due course. The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. Its inaugural meeting was held on August 31 in Istanbul, where it was decided that a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. The secretariat will initially be headed by a secretary general from Pakistan for a period of three years. ‘State-sanctioned’ demolition of Muslim worship sites in India condemned The FO spokesperson also condemned what he described as the “systematic” and “state-sanctioned” demolition of Muslim worship sites in India. In response to a question about how Pakistan planned to build more pressure on the Indian government regarding the issue of demolition of worship sites, given the demolition of a mosque in India’s Saharanpur on September 5, the spokesperson said, “Pakistan expresses deep concern and condemns the systematic state-sanctioned demolition of Islamic holy places in India under different pretexts”. Khan held that the demolitions were in breach of the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed in 1950, which the spokesperson said guaranteed the security and rights of religious minorities. He noted that the ongoing repression also breached India’s own laws, particularly the Places of Worship Special Provisions Act, 1991, which he said mandated the maintenance of the religious character of places of worship “as it existed on August 15, 1947”. Referring to the recent demolition of a mosque in Uttar Pradesh, he noted: “The Hindu-driven Islamophobic campaign has resulted in an imminent threat and the destruction of centuries-old heritage sites and places of worship, including the Akhonji, Ajgaib Shaeed Mosque, the Saharanapur Collectorate mosque, as well as the 1,000-year-old mosque, Ganj Shahida mosque, which has recently received notices from the court.” He recalled that the 1992 demolition of the Babri mosque remained a “dreadful memory of this ideology of religious intolerance, prejudice, and hatred”. Explaining what steps Pakistan planned to take towards the issue, Khan said, “Pakistan calls upon the international community to take immediate notice of this systematic persecution in India against Muslims and continued desecration and destruction of their places of worship”. In the weekly briefing, Khan also issued a categorical rejection of a statement made by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs over a Hindu temple in Narowal . “Contrary to India’s claim, the temple’s structure was damaged in torrential rain,” he said. Yasin Malik’s decision to forgo defence ‘damning indictment’ of Indian judicial system The spokesperson was also asked about the recent implication of the Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF)’s incarcerated chairman, Muhammad Yasin Malik, in a case from 1990. Malik was named in June by India’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) as one of five men charged with the killing of Sarla Bhat. However, he submitted an affidavit stating that he had decided not to contest the trial and that his decision should not be treated as an admission of guilt or acceptance of the prosecution’s allegations. Referring to Malik’s action, the FO said, “The stance taken by Yasin Malik is beyond an act of heroism. It is a damning indictment of the Indian judicial system, which has acted as a convenient tool in the hands of the Indian government, suppressing the Kashmiri people and depriving them of any recourse to justice”. Khan held that in repudiating the right to defence, Malik has “struck a stinging blow to the judicial sham that the Indian government wanted to stage in its sinister campaign to malign the Kashmiri leadership”. The spokesperson also expressed concern at Malik’s deteriorating health. “The international community must not allow the Indian design to mortgage his life and well-being to advance its oppressive occupation of the IIOK,” he said, adding that Pakistan condemned the prosecution of Malik. The FO spokesperson urged the UN and other humanitarian bodies to take note of Malik’s situation.

items.title: Why we dispersed ADC supporters – Kaduna police
items.description: The Police Command in Kaduna has explained the circumstances surrounding the dispersal of a crowd carrying African Democratic Congress, ADC, banners in Kaduna metropolis. Read Also: Obi denies rejecting Atiku’s VP offer A statement by Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Mansir Hassan, on Thursday in Kaduna said the incident occurred on Wednesday following a distress call from security personnel attached to Murtala Square, that some persons were attempting to forcefully gain entry into the premises. He said police personnel were immediately deployed to the location to prevent a breach of security and maintain public order. According to him, on arrival, the police observed a large number of persons carrying banners bearing the acronym “ADC”. He said the police advised the group that anyone intending to hold an event or gain access to Murtala Square was required to follow due process and obtain the necessary authorisation from the management. Hassan said the police subsequently withdrew from the area after the situation appeared to have been brought under control. He, however, said the group later proceeded along WAFF Road towards NEPA Roundabout by Ahmadu Bello Way, one of the major commercial routes in the metropolis. “The protesters blocked the roadway, resulting in severe traffic congestion and bringing vehicular movement to a standstill,” he said. The PPRO said the obstruction led to frustration among the group, cyclists and motorists, resulting in agitation, confrontation and a breakdown of public order. He said the police intervened to restore normalcy and prevent further escalation, adding that minimal and proportionate force, including tear gas, was used to disperse the crowd. Hassan said the command respected the constitutional rights of citizens to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association. He, however, stressed that such rights must be exercised responsibly and within the ambit of the law. He said citizens should not obstruct major public roads, threaten public safety or infringe on the rights of other members of the public. The PPRO also clarified that the command had never attempted to stop any lawful political gathering or peaceful assembly. He said the incident was a security situation at Murtala Square and not an attempt by the police to prevent political expression or association. Hassan urged members of the public to disregard what he described as misleading narratives surrounding the incident and rely on verified information from the command. items.title: England dominate Pakistan, close in on Test series sweep
items.description: Ruthless England tamed Pakistan’s inexperienced attack in the third Test at Edgbaston on Thursday to move to the brink of a series whitewash against their hapless opponents. Joe Root’s men, already 2-0 up in the three-match contest, were dismissed for 453 on the second day of the match to take a first-innings lead of 320, threatening to wrap up victory in double-quick time. England rattled along on a sunny morning in Birmingham, with Dan Lawrence reaching his half-century off just 47 balls, hitting eight fours. But their progress was checked when Harry Brook needlessly ran himself out for 75 when in sight of an 11th Test century. Brook tossed his bat into the air in frustration as his partnership with Lawrence was ended at 86, leaving England 229-5. The scoring slowed briefly after Jamie Smith arrived at the crease but he soon showed his attacking intent, launching the ball straight back over the head of spinner Saim Ayub for six. Lawrence (65) chopped a ball from Mohammad Imran onto his stumps shortly before lunch to give the all-rounder his first Test wicket. Gus Atkinson was bowled by Imran for 19 but, as the clouds rolled in, the home side maintained the momentum established by the middle and lower orders. Smith’s promising innings ended with a whimper when he was caught and bowled for 69 by Razaullah, who celebrated his third wicket on his Test debut with gusto. But Ollie Robinson hit 50 off 47 balls and fellow paceman Jofra Archer smashed a quickfire 32 to heap more pain on Pakistan. Razaullah finished as the pick of the bowlers, with figures of 4-148. The tourists are seeking to avoid a 16th Test defeat in 21 matches at the end of a turbulent tour. They released seven players and sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul after their 194-run defeat in the second Test, making four changes to their side in Birmingham. But their new-look team were dismissed for a paltry 133, failing to reach 200 for the fifth consecutive innings in England, with none of the top five making double figures. Pakistan reduced England to 39-3 but opener Emilio Gay scored 60 on Wednesday to settle their nerves before he was dismissed. A 3-0 win at the start of Root’s second stint as the permanent skipper would be a huge boost for a side that was in turmoil just weeks ago following a series loss to New Zealand and the exits of head coach Brendon McCullum and captain Ben Stokes.

items.title: Liaison à 100 Gbit/s et construction d'un centre de formation professionnelle : l'Algérie et le Niger renforcent leur partenariat
items.description: Les operateurs de telecommunications algerien et nigerien, Algerie Telecom et Niger Telecom, ont signe le 8 septembre des accords de cooperation entre les deux entreprises et l'ecole superieure des communications electroniques et des services postaux (ESCEP-Niger) du Niger. Ces accords ont ete signes par la representante du directeur general d'Algerie Telecom, Amina Dahdouh, le directeur general de l'ESCEP-Niger, Abdoul Salam Koroney, et le directeur general de Niger Telecom, Amadou Abdou Abdourahamane. Coopération: Algérie Télécom signe deux conventions de partenariat avec Niger Télécom et ESCEP-Niger La société Algérie Télécoms a signé, ce mardi 08 septembre 2026 à Niamey, des accords de partenariat avec Niger Télécom et avec l’Ecole Supérieure des Communications… pic.twitter.com/npdPSsQy1z — Niger Fr (@NigerAr) September 8, 2026 L'accord entre Algerie Telecom et Niger Telecom prevoit la construction d'une ligne de communication terrestre a fibre optique entre les deux pays, d'une capacite initiale de 100 Gbit/s. Ce projet prevoit la fourniture par Algerie Telecom d'equipements de transmission destines a la mise en place de cette ligne de communication entre In-Gezzam (Algerie) et Agadez (Niger). Une fois mise en service, celle-ci devrait renforcer la capacite du reseau national dorsal existant de Niger Telecom, en y ajoutant une nouvelle liaison internationale. De plus, un autre accord entre Algerie Telecom et Niger Telecom porte sur la formation du personnel des operateurs nigeriens et la formation des formateurs. Parallelement, Algerie Telecom et l'ecole superieure des communications electroniques et des services postaux ont conclu un accord de partenariat visant a creer un Centre de formation professionnelle au sein de l'ESCEP-Niger, qui aura pour objectif de former des specialistes dans le domaine des technologies numeriques. Le secretaire general du ministere nigerien de la Communication et des Nouvelles Technologies de l'Information,M. Mashoul Abdoul Nasser a salue la solidite et la vitalite des relations d'amitie et de cooperation qui unissent l'Algerie et le Niger. D'apres lui, la visite au Niger de la delegation algerienne « temoigne egalement de la volonte partagee de notre Gouvernement de consolider un partenariat fonde sur le respect mutuel, la confiance et l'interet reciproques de nos deux peuples ». Pour sa part, Ameena Dahdouh a declare que les liens qui unissent l'Algerie et le Niger ne sont pas nes aujourd'hui. « Ils s'enracinent dans une histoire commune, une proximite geographique et une solidarite que nos deux peuples n'ont cesse de cultiver », a-t-elle affirme. La cooperation entre l'Algerie et le Niger s'etend egalement a d'autres domaines. Debut septembre, Alger et Niamey ont renforce leur partenariat dans le secteur energetique autour du bloc petrolier de Bilma. La societe Sonatrach devrait revoir l'etude de faisabilite du projet, dont la production, selon les estimations de la presse, pourrait depasser 20 000 barils par jour pendant une vingtaine d'annees.

items.title: Ghana to pre-qualify local companies to manufacture vaccines for African market
items.description: Chief Executive Officer of the National Vaccine Institute (NVI), Dr Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, has disclosed that Ghana is preparing to pre-qualify Ghanaian companies to manufacture vaccines for the local and wider African market. He said the move follows Ghana’s decision to join the Africa Pool Procurement Mechanism, which is expected to create opportunities for local vaccine manufacturers to compete for supply contracts across the continent. Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Thursday, September 10, Dr Sodzi-Tettey confirmed that Ghana’s plan is to manufacture and supply selected vaccines rather than simply import them. “That is the plan,” he said when asked whether a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed by Ghana would eventually lead to the country manufacturing and supplying certain vaccines. He said a regional meeting would be held in Accra in November to begin the process of identifying and preparing Ghanaian companies that have the capacity to participate. “So in November this year, having joined the Africa pool procurement mechanism, we are going to organise a regional meeting. We will have the leadership of the pool procurement mechanism in Accra,” he said. According to Dr Sodzi-Tettey, the meeting will launch an application process through which Ghanaian companies will be assessed and pre-qualified. “What they are going to do is roll out an application process that would enable us to pre-qualify Ghanaian companies,” he explained. He said interested companies would have to demonstrate their manufacturing capacity, including the type and volume of vaccines they can produce. “So the companies will have to demonstrate capacity. What are you able to manufacture and in what quantities?” he said. Companies that successfully pass the pre-selection process will then be able to participate in tenders and potentially supply vaccines beyond Ghana. “Once you are pre-selected, it means that when the tenders are issued, you can apply, and then you can have access to the continental market of over 1.4 billion people,” Dr Sodzi-Tettey said. Dr Sodzi-Tettey was also asked why Ghana had settled on five vaccines for the initial phase of its manufacturing plans. He explained that the selection was based on the importance of the vaccines to the country’s immunisation programme. “So we settled on them because they are critical for our vaccine immunisation programme,” he said. He also cited incentives available under the Gavi-supported Africa Vaccines Manufacturing Accelerator initiative, which aims to encourage vaccine production in Africa, particularly in areas requiring more complex manufacturing capabilities. “We settled on them also because within Gavi, there are some incentives. There’s a programme called Africa Vaccines Manufacturing Accelerator Initiative where there are some incentives that are put there for more complex manufacturing,” he said. He said those incentives could help manufacturers recover the significant investments required to produce more complex vaccines. “Which means that when we are able to hit those areas, we would be able to recoup our investments into those areas,” he said. Dr Sodzi-Tettey said Ghana would initially focus on a product that does not receive such subsidies before moving into more complex vaccine manufacturing. “So we started with a product that has no subsidies, so to speak,” he said. He added that the expectation was for governments to provide a market for the initial products, allowing local manufacturers to build their capacity before expanding into more complex production. “But we think that the governments are able to purchase that and then we go into more complex manufacturing, which we can then supply to the rest of the market,” he said. While the initial manufacturing programme will focus on vaccines that are already established, Dr Sodzi-Tettey said Ghana is also looking at research and development for diseases for which there are currently no established vaccines. “So, the manufacturing is now focusing on established vaccines,” he said. He explained that research would focus on developing new vaccine candidates to respond to emerging diseases and future health threats. “And then there’s the work being done in research and development to develop new vaccine candidates, to manage things like mpox, Ebola, and so on and so on, which we do not have established vaccines for yet,” he said. “That is where the research will be focused on developing new vaccines.”
